contents.title: Master PostgreSQL with TypeORM
contents.description: Learn how to define Entities, set up One-to-One, One-to-Many, and Many-to-Many relationships, and integrate TypeORM with PostgreSQL in NestJS.
contents.body:
## I. Introduction

Many developers working with relational databases write long raw **SQL** statements directly for table creation, querying, and updates. This is time-consuming and error-prone, especially as systems grow with many linked tables.

**TypeORM** addresses this by letting you define **Entities** in TypeScript, then translating them into corresponding **SQL** operations behind the scenes. This lesson helps you use TypeORM to manage schema, model relationships, and operate data in a structured way.

## II. Essence

This lesson follows a **source-first** approach: read the real flow `Entity -> Service -> Repository`, then test APIs to see exactly how TypeORM maps TypeScript classes to PostgreSQL tables and handles relationships.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql)

### Runtime Dependency Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> CatsController[CatsController]
    CatsController --> CatsService[CatsService]
    CatsService --> CatRepo[Repository<CatEntity>]
    CatRepo --> CatEntity[CatEntity + relations]
    CatRepo --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
```

### Source Code Tree (File Level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "app.module.ts"
        "modules"
            "cats"
                "cats.module.ts"
                "cats.controller.ts"
                "cats.service.ts"
                "entities"
                    "cat.entity.ts"
                    "cat-passport.entity.ts"
                    "toy.entity.ts"
                    "owner.entity.ts"
                "dto/create-cat.dto.ts"
```

### Environment Setup and Run Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** Require `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop, and git.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source to work in the right context:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Start PostgreSQL:** Run the database container:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f .docker/postgresql.yaml up --build -d
  ```
- **4. Install dependencies and run app:** Install packages and start dev server:
  ```bash
  npm install
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** App starts on port `3000`; TypeORM creates tables `cats`, `toys`, `owners`, `cat_passports`.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Create a new cat with cascade relationships.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - create cat with relations - POST http://localhost:3000/cats**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `POST` to `http://localhost:3000/cats`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "name": "Tom",
    "age": 3,
    "passport": { "issuedAt": "2024-01-01" },
    "toys": [{ "name": "Ball" }],
    "owners": [{ "name": "Alice" }]
  }
  ```

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/cats \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"Tom","age":3,"passport":{"issuedAt":"2024-01-01"},"toys":[{"name":"Ball"}],"owners":[{"name":"Alice"}]}'
  ```

- **Step 2:** Read cat details to confirm relations were persisted.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - get one cat with relations - GET http://localhost:3000/cats/1**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `GET` to `http://localhost:3000/cats/1`.

  **JSON Body:** No body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/1
  ```

  **Trace code execution (by file):**
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:24`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L24) -> `CatsController.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:29`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L29) -> `CatsService.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/entities/cat.entity.ts:11`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/entities/cat.entity.ts#L11) -> `CatEntity` relation decorators
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:53`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L53) -> `CatsService.findOne()`

  *Expected result:* Returned data includes the cat and saved relations (`passport`, `toys`, `owners`) correctly.

  *Conclusion:* TypeORM reduces manual SQL through entity/relation mapping while preserving relational integrity on PostgreSQL.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Entity Mapping***

- **Role:** `@Entity`, `@Column` map TypeScript classes to PostgreSQL tables/columns.
- **Common mistake:** Declaring column types that do not match real data.
- **Production impact:** Type-cast query errors and risky migrations.

### 2. ***Relation Mapping***

- **Role:** `@OneToOne`, `@OneToMany`, `@ManyToMany` express domain relationships clearly.
- **Common mistake:** Setting overly broad cascade rules and unintentionally overwriting linked data.
- **Production impact:** Related data mutates in hard-to-control ways.

### 3. ***Indexing***

- **Role:** Speed up queries on frequently filtered/sorted columns.
- **Common mistake:** Missing indexes on hot query columns or over-indexing every column.
- **Production impact:** Slow reads or slow writes due to index maintenance overhead.

### 4. ***Transaction***

- **Role:** Ensure grouped DB operations all succeed or all rollback.
- **Common mistake:** Splitting multi-step writes without transaction boundaries.
- **Production impact:** Partial data states and business inconsistency.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

**TypeORM** becomes most powerful when used with deliberate architecture decisions: define aggregate boundaries for safe cascade usage, index based on real query patterns, and wrap critical write workflows in transactions.

In production, combining these techniques with migration discipline and query profiling helps you keep PostgreSQL both consistent and performant as data volume grows.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   “In TypeORM, when should you enable `cascade: true`, and when should you avoid it?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Understanding relation lifecycle and chain-write risks.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Use cascade for clear aggregate boundaries; avoid blind cascade on shared relations to prevent accidental writes.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   “Why can querying by `name` be slow even with only a few hundred thousand records?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to read execution plans and reason about indexing.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Point out missing/ineffective index possibilities; propose adding the correct index and measuring again.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   “How do you implement a transfer A -> B with TypeORM so data is never lost on mid-flow failure?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to apply transactions in critical business workflows.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Use transactions (`QueryRunner`/transaction manager) and rollback if any step fails.

  **Hướng dẫn gọi API:** Dùng Postman gửi `GET` tới `http://localhost:3000/cats/1`.

  **Body JSON:** Không có body với request `GET`.

  Hoặc dùng **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/1
  ```

  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:24`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L24) -> `CatsController.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:29`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L29) -> `CatsService.create()`

  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:53`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L53) -> `CatsService.findOne()`

  *Kết luận:* TypeORM giảm SQL thủ công bằng mapping entity/relation, đồng thời vẫn giữ được tính toàn vẹn quan hệ trên PostgreSQL.

## III. Các khái niệm cốt lõi

### 1. ***Entity Mapping***

- **Vai trò:** `@Entity`, `@Column` ánh xạ class TypeScript thành bảng/cột PostgreSQL.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Khai báo kiểu cột không khớp dữ liệu thực tế.
- **Hậu quả production:** Query lỗi cast type, migration phát sinh rủi ro.

### 2. ***Relation Mapping***

- **Vai trò:** `@OneToOne`, `@OneToMany`, `@ManyToMany` mô tả quan hệ domain rõ ràng.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Đặt cascade quá rộng, ghi đè dữ liệu liên kết ngoài ý muốn.
- **Hậu quả production:** Dữ liệu liên đới bị mutate khó kiểm soát.

### 3. ***Indexing***

- **Vai trò:** Tăng tốc truy vấn cho các cột filter/sort thường dùng.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Quên index cột truy vấn nóng hoặc lạm dụng index trên mọi cột.
- **Hậu quả production:** Chậm đọc hoặc chậm ghi do index maintenance quá nặng.

### 4. ***Transaction***

- **Vai trò:** Đảm bảo nhóm thao tác DB thành công toàn bộ hoặc rollback toàn bộ.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Chia nhiều thao tác ghi mà không bọc transaction.
- **Hậu quả production:** Trạng thái dữ liệu dở dang, sai lệch nghiệp vụ.

## IV. Kết luận

**TypeORM** là cầu nối mạnh mẽ giữa **TypeScript** và **PostgreSQL**, giúp bạn định nghĩa schema bằng code, thiết lập quan hệ bằng decorator và tối ưu truy vấn bằng indexing. Cascade save đơn giản hóa việc thao tác dữ liệu phức tạp, trong khi Transaction đảm bảo tính toàn vẹn tuyệt đối.

**Kết luận:** Làm chủ TypeORM không chỉ là biết viết Entity — mà là hiểu cách thiết kế quan hệ, tối ưu hiệu năng và đảm bảo dữ liệu luôn nhất quán trong mọi tình huống.

## V. Các mẫu câu phỏng vấn

1. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Trong TypeORM, khi nào nên bật `cascade: true` và khi nào nên tránh?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Mức độ hiểu về lifecycle relation và rủi ro ghi dữ liệu dây chuyền.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Dùng cascade cho aggregate boundary rõ ràng; tránh cascade mù ở quan hệ shared để không ghi nhầm dữ liệu.

2. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Vì sao query theo `name` chậm dù dữ liệu chỉ vài trăm nghìn bản ghi?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Năng lực đọc execution plan và tư duy index.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Chỉ ra khả năng thiếu index hoặc dùng index không hiệu quả; đề xuất thêm index đúng cột và đo lại.

3. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Bạn xử lý chuyển tiền A -> B bằng TypeORM như thế nào để không mất dữ liệu khi lỗi giữa chừng?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Khả năng áp dụng transaction trong nghiệp vụ quan trọng.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Dùng transaction (`QueryRunner`/manager transaction), rollback nếu bất kỳ bước nào thất bại.
Master PostgreSQL with TypeORM
Learn how to define Entities, set up One-to-One, One-to-Many, and Many-to-Many relationships, and integrate TypeORM with PostgreSQL in NestJS.

## I. Introduction

Many developers working with relational databases write long raw **SQL** statements directly for table creation, querying, and updates. This is time-consuming and error-prone, especially as systems grow with many linked tables.

**TypeORM** addresses this by letting you define **Entities** in TypeScript, then translating them into corresponding **SQL** operations behind the scenes. This lesson helps you use TypeORM to manage schema, model relationships, and operate data in a structured way.

## II. Essence

This lesson follows a **source-first** approach: read the real flow `Entity -> Service -> Repository`, then test APIs to see exactly how TypeORM maps TypeScript classes to PostgreSQL tables and handles relationships.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql)

### Runtime Dependency Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> CatsController[CatsController]
    CatsController --> CatsService[CatsService]
    CatsService --> CatRepo[Repository<CatEntity>]
    CatRepo --> CatEntity[CatEntity + relations]
    CatRepo --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
```

### Source Code Tree (File Level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "app.module.ts"
        "modules"
            "cats"
                "cats.module.ts"
                "cats.controller.ts"
                "cats.service.ts"
                "entities"
                    "cat.entity.ts"
                    "cat-passport.entity.ts"
                    "toy.entity.ts"
                    "owner.entity.ts"
                "dto/create-cat.dto.ts"
```

### Environment Setup and Run Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** Require `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop, and git.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source to work in the right context:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Start PostgreSQL:** Run the database container:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f .docker/postgresql.yaml up --build -d
  ```
- **4. Install dependencies and run app:** Install packages and start dev server:
  ```bash
  npm install
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** App starts on port `3000`; TypeORM creates tables `cats`, `toys`, `owners`, `cat_passports`.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Create a new cat with cascade relationships.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - create cat with relations - POST http://localhost:3000/cats**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `POST` to `http://localhost:3000/cats`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "name": "Tom",
    "age": 3,
    "passport": { "issuedAt": "2024-01-01" },
    "toys": [{ "name": "Ball" }],
    "owners": [{ "name": "Alice" }]
  }
  ```

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/cats \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"Tom","age":3,"passport":{"issuedAt":"2024-01-01"},"toys":[{"name":"Ball"}],"owners":[{"name":"Alice"}]}'
  ```

- **Step 2:** Read cat details to confirm relations were persisted.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - get one cat with relations - GET http://localhost:3000/cats/1**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `GET` to `http://localhost:3000/cats/1`.

  **JSON Body:** No body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/1
  ```

  **Trace code execution (by file):**
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:24`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L24) -> `CatsController.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:29`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L29) -> `CatsService.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/entities/cat.entity.ts:11`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/entities/cat.entity.ts#L11) -> `CatEntity` relation decorators
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:53`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L53) -> `CatsService.findOne()`

  *Expected result:* Returned data includes the cat and saved relations (`passport`, `toys`, `owners`) correctly.

  *Conclusion:* TypeORM reduces manual SQL through entity/relation mapping while preserving relational integrity on PostgreSQL.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Entity Mapping***

- **Role:** `@Entity`, `@Column` map TypeScript classes to PostgreSQL tables/columns.
- **Common mistake:** Declaring column types that do not match real data.
- **Production impact:** Type-cast query errors and risky migrations.

### 2. ***Relation Mapping***

- **Role:** `@OneToOne`, `@OneToMany`, `@ManyToMany` express domain relationships clearly.
- **Common mistake:** Setting overly broad cascade rules and unintentionally overwriting linked data.
- **Production impact:** Related data mutates in hard-to-control ways.

### 3. ***Indexing***

- **Role:** Speed up queries on frequently filtered/sorted columns.
- **Common mistake:** Missing indexes on hot query columns or over-indexing every column.
- **Production impact:** Slow reads or slow writes due to index maintenance overhead.

### 4. ***Transaction***

- **Role:** Ensure grouped DB operations all succeed or all rollback.
- **Common mistake:** Splitting multi-step writes without transaction boundaries.
- **Production impact:** Partial data states and business inconsistency.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

**TypeORM** becomes most powerful when used with deliberate architecture decisions: define aggregate boundaries for safe cascade usage, index based on real query patterns, and wrap critical write workflows in transactions.

In production, combining these techniques with migration discipline and query profiling helps you keep PostgreSQL both consistent and performant as data volume grows.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   “In TypeORM, when should you enable `cascade: true`, and when should you avoid it?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Understanding relation lifecycle and chain-write risks.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Use cascade for clear aggregate boundaries; avoid blind cascade on shared relations to prevent accidental writes.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   “Why can querying by `name` be slow even with only a few hundred thousand records?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to read execution plans and reason about indexing.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Point out missing/ineffective index possibilities; propose adding the correct index and measuring again.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   “How do you implement a transfer A -> B with TypeORM so data is never lost on mid-flow failure?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to apply transactions in critical business workflows.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Use transactions (`QueryRunner`/transaction manager) and rollback if any step fails.

contents.title: NoSQL Storage with MongoDB and Mongoose
contents.description: Learn how to use Mongoose ODM in NestJS to define schemas, create indexes, manage timestamps, and work with MongoDB documents in a disciplined way.
contents.body:
## I. Introduction

When working with **MongoDB**, many beginners assume NoSQL means total freedom: no schema and no constraints. As systems grow, that assumption quickly leads to inconsistent data: a field exists in one document but is missing in another, and data types drift over time.

**Mongoose** solves this by adding an application-layer discipline. It enforces a defined **Schema** before documents are persisted, so you keep MongoDB flexibility without sacrificing data consistency.

## II. Essence

This lesson follows a **source-first** approach: read the Mongoose schema and service first, then test the API to see how MongoDB remains flexible while still guarded by validation and schema rules.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb)

### Runtime Dependency Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> CatsController[CatsController]
    CatsController --> CatsService[CatsService]
    CatsService --> CatModel[Mongoose Model<CatDocument>]
    CatModel --> CatSchema[CatSchema + indexes + timestamps]
    CatModel --> MDB[(MongoDB)]
```

### Source Code Tree (file-level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "app.module.ts"
        "modules"
            "cats"
                "cats.module.ts"
                "cats.controller.ts"
                "cats.service.ts"
                "schemas"
                    "cat.schema.ts"
                "dto"
                    "create-cat.dto.ts"
                    "update-cat.dto.ts"
```

### Environment Setup and Run Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop, and Git are required.
- **2. Clone the demo source:** Clone/pull the source so your code context matches:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Start MongoDB:** Run the MongoDB container:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f .docker/mongodb.yaml up --build -d
  ```
- **4. Install dependencies and run the app:** Install packages and start the server:
  ```bash
  npm install
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** The app runs on port `3000`; newly created documents include `createdAt` and `updatedAt`.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Create a cat document with flexible metadata.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - create document - POST http://localhost:3000/cats**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send a `POST` request to `http://localhost:3000/cats`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "name": "Tom",
    "age": 3,
    "metadata": { "color": "orange", "weight": 4.5 },
    "hobbies": ["sleeping", "playing"]
  }
  ```

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/cats \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"Tom","age":3,"metadata":{"color":"orange","weight":4.5},"hobbies":["sleeping","playing"]}'
  ```

- **Step 2:** Update a document by id and observe how `updatedAt` changes.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - patch cat age - PATCH http://localhost:3000/cats/{id}**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send a `PATCH` request to `http://localhost:3000/cats/{id}`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "age": 4
  }
  ```

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3000/cats/REPLACE_ID \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"age":4}'
  ```

  **Trace code execution (by file):**
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:21`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L21) -> `CatsController.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:18`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L18) -> `CatsService.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/schemas/cat.schema.ts:9`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/schemas/cat.schema.ts#L9) -> `CatSchema` (`required`, `index`, `timestamps`)
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:41`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L41) -> `CatsService.update()`

  *Expected result:* Data is stored as flexible documents while validation enforces minimum consistency for critical fields.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Schema Discipline***

- **Role:** Mongoose schemas define a minimum data contract before documents are written.
- **Common mistake:** Assuming NoSQL means skipping validation entirely.
- **Production impact:** Inconsistent structures make querying and migration difficult.

### 2. ***MongoDB Indexing***

- **Role:** Indexes speed up queries on frequently filtered fields.
- **Common mistake:** Skipping indexes on hot fields like `name`, `email`, or `slug`.
- **Production impact:** Full collection scans and high latency at scale.

### 3. ***Flexible Fields***

- **Role:** `Object` and `Array` fields support flexible metadata/hobby storage without frequent migrations.
- **Common mistake:** Overusing free-form fields without an API contract.
- **Production impact:** Frontend/backend expectation mismatches and serialization bugs.

### 4. ***Query API and `.exec()`***

- **Role:** `.exec()` returns explicit Promises, making async flow and error handling clearer.
- **Common mistake:** Mixing callbacks, query objects, and `await` inconsistently.
- **Production impact:** Unpredictable error flow and difficult runtime tracing.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

For larger systems, combine schema validation with stronger patterns: add compound indexes for common filter/sort combinations, use partial indexes for sparse fields, and define DTO-level contracts that align with flexible document fields. This keeps read performance predictable while preserving MongoDB agility.

**Conclusion:** MongoDB is powerful not because it ignores schema, but because it allows flexible storage while Mongoose enforces discipline at the application boundary.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   "Why use Mongoose schemas in production even when using MongoDB?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Understanding the trade-off between flexibility and data discipline.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Explain that schemas enforce validation, standardize fields, reduce dirty data, and stabilize API behavior.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   "What value does `timestamps: true` provide in debugging and data auditing?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Observability and incident analysis mindset.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Use `createdAt/updatedAt` to trace changes, detect stale records, and investigate abnormal updates.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   "When should you store a list as an embedded array versus a separate collection?"
   - **What is being assessed:** MongoDB data modeling by access pattern.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Embed when data is read together and bounded in size; split when growth or independent querying becomes significant.

  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:18`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L18) -> `CatsService.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/schemas/cat.schema.ts:9`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/schemas/cat.schema.ts#L9) -> `CatSchema` (`required`, `index`, `timestamps`)
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:41`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L41) -> `CatsService.update()`

  *Kết quả mong đợi:* Dữ liệu được lưu dạng document linh hoạt, validation giữ tính nhất quán tối thiểu ở các trường quan trọng.

  *Kết luận:* MongoDB + Mongoose phù hợp bài toán schema biến động nhanh nhưng vẫn cần guardrail ở tầng ứng dụng.

## III. Các khái niệm cốt lõi

### 1. ***Schema Discipline***

- **Vai trò:** Mongoose schema tạo chuẩn dữ liệu tối thiểu trước khi ghi document.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Hiểu nhầm NoSQL là bỏ validation hoàn toàn.
- **Hậu quả production:** Dữ liệu lệch cấu trúc, khó query và khó migrate.

### 2. ***Index trong MongoDB***

- **Vai trò:** Tăng tốc truy vấn cho các field tìm kiếm thường xuyên.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Không tạo index cho field nóng như `name`, `email`, `slug`.
- **Hậu quả production:** Full collection scan, latency tăng mạnh khi dữ liệu lớn.

### 3. ***Flexible Fields***

- **Vai trò:** `Object` và `Array` giúp lưu metadata/hobbies linh hoạt không cần migration dày đặc.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Lạm dụng field tự do mà không có contract API.
- **Hậu quả production:** Frontend/backend lệch kỳ vọng dữ liệu, bug serialization.

### 4. ***Query API và `.exec()`***

- **Vai trò:** `.exec()` trả Promise rõ ràng, dễ quản trị async flow và error handling.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Trộn callback, query object và await không nhất quán.
- **Hậu quả production:** Luồng lỗi khó đoán, khó trace nguyên nhân runtime.

## IV. Kết luận

**Mongoose** mang lại sự cân bằng hoàn hảo giữa tính linh hoạt của **MongoDB** và tính kỷ luật của schema. Với khả năng định nghĩa **index**, **timestamps**, và lưu trữ dữ liệu dạng **Object** và **Array** trực tiếp trong document, Mongoose là lựa chọn lý tưởng cho các dự án cần tốc độ phát triển nhanh nhưng vẫn đảm bảo chất lượng dữ liệu.

**Kết luận:** Sức mạnh của MongoDB không phải là "không cần schema" — mà là khả năng lưu trữ dữ liệu linh hoạt trong khi vẫn được Mongoose bảo vệ bằng lớp validation nghiêm ngặt ở tầng ứng dụng.

## V. Các mẫu câu phỏng vấn

1. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Tại sao dùng MongoDB nhưng vẫn cần Mongoose schema trong dự án production?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Hiểu trade-off giữa linh hoạt và kỷ luật dữ liệu.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Nêu schema giúp validation, chuẩn field, giảm dữ liệu bẩn và tăng tính ổn định API.

2. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “`timestamps: true` có giá trị gì khi phân tích lỗi hoặc audit dữ liệu?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Tư duy observability và điều tra sự cố.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Dùng `createdAt/updatedAt` để truy vết lịch sử thay đổi, xác định bản ghi stale hoặc cập nhật bất thường.

3. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Khi nào nên lưu danh sách dưới dạng embedded array trong document, khi nào nên tách collection?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Khả năng thiết kế data model MongoDB theo access pattern.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Embed khi đọc cùng nhau, kích thước vừa phải; tách collection khi dữ liệu tăng lớn hoặc cần truy vấn độc lập nhiều chiều.
NoSQL Storage with MongoDB and Mongoose
Learn how to use Mongoose ODM in NestJS to define schemas, create indexes, manage timestamps, and work with MongoDB documents in a disciplined way.

## I. Introduction

When working with **MongoDB**, many beginners assume NoSQL means total freedom: no schema and no constraints. As systems grow, that assumption quickly leads to inconsistent data: a field exists in one document but is missing in another, and data types drift over time.

**Mongoose** solves this by adding an application-layer discipline. It enforces a defined **Schema** before documents are persisted, so you keep MongoDB flexibility without sacrificing data consistency.

## II. Essence

This lesson follows a **source-first** approach: read the Mongoose schema and service first, then test the API to see how MongoDB remains flexible while still guarded by validation and schema rules.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb)

### Runtime Dependency Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> CatsController[CatsController]
    CatsController --> CatsService[CatsService]
    CatsService --> CatModel[Mongoose Model<CatDocument>]
    CatModel --> CatSchema[CatSchema + indexes + timestamps]
    CatModel --> MDB[(MongoDB)]
```

### Source Code Tree (file-level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta

        "app.module.ts"
        "modules"
            "cats"
                "cats.module.ts"
                "cats.controller.ts"
                "cats.service.ts"
                "schemas"

                "dto"
                    "create-cat.dto.ts"
                    "update-cat.dto.ts"
```

### Environment Setup and Run Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop, and Git are required.
- **2. Clone the demo source:** Clone/pull the source so your code context matches:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Start MongoDB:** Run the MongoDB container:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f .docker/mongodb.yaml up --build -d
  ```
- **4. Install dependencies and run the app:** Install packages and start the server:
  ```bash
  npm install
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** The app runs on port `3000`; newly created documents include `createdAt` and `updatedAt`.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Create a cat document with flexible metadata.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - create document - POST http://localhost:3000/cats**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send a `POST` request to `http://localhost:3000/cats`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "name": "Tom",
    "age": 3,
    "metadata": { "color": "orange", "weight": 4.5 },
    "hobbies": ["sleeping", "playing"]
  }
  ```

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/cats \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"Tom","age":3,"metadata":{"color":"orange","weight":4.5},"hobbies":["sleeping","playing"]}'
  ```

- **Step 2:** Update a document by id and observe how `updatedAt` changes.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - patch cat age - PATCH http://localhost:3000/cats/{id}**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send a `PATCH` request to `http://localhost:3000/cats/{id}`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "age": 4
  }
  ```

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3000/cats/REPLACE_ID \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"age":4}'
  ```

  **Trace code execution (by file):**
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:21`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L21) -> `CatsController.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:18`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L18) -> `CatsService.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/schemas/cat.schema.ts:9`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/schemas/cat.schema.ts#L9) -> `CatSchema` (`required`, `index`, `timestamps`)
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:41`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L41) -> `CatsService.update()`

  *Expected result:* Data is stored as flexible documents while validation enforces minimum consistency for critical fields.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Schema Discipline***

- **Role:** Mongoose schemas define a minimum data contract before documents are written.
- **Common mistake:** Assuming NoSQL means skipping validation entirely.
- **Production impact:** Inconsistent structures make querying and migration difficult.

### 2. ***MongoDB Indexing***

- **Role:** Indexes speed up queries on frequently filtered fields.
- **Common mistake:** Skipping indexes on hot fields like `name`, `email`, or `slug`.
- **Production impact:** Full collection scans and high latency at scale.

### 3. ***Flexible Fields***

- **Role:** `Object` and `Array` fields support flexible metadata/hobby storage without frequent migrations.
- **Common mistake:** Overusing free-form fields without an API contract.
- **Production impact:** Frontend/backend expectation mismatches and serialization bugs.

### 4. ***Query API and `.exec()`***

- **Role:** `.exec()` returns explicit Promises, making async flow and error handling clearer.
- **Common mistake:** Mixing callbacks, query objects, and `await` inconsistently.
- **Production impact:** Unpredictable error flow and difficult runtime tracing.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

For larger systems, combine schema validation with stronger patterns: add compound indexes for common filter/sort combinations, use partial indexes for sparse fields, and define DTO-level contracts that align with flexible document fields. This keeps read performance predictable while preserving MongoDB agility.

**Conclusion:** MongoDB is powerful not because it ignores schema, but because it allows flexible storage while Mongoose enforces discipline at the application boundary.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   "Why use Mongoose schemas in production even when using MongoDB?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Understanding the trade-off between flexibility and data discipline.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Explain that schemas enforce validation, standardize fields, reduce dirty data, and stabilize API behavior.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   "What value does `timestamps: true` provide in debugging and data auditing?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Observability and incident analysis mindset.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Use `createdAt/updatedAt` to trace changes, detect stale records, and investigate abnormal updates.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   "When should you store a list as an embedded array versus a separate collection?"
   - **What is being assessed:** MongoDB data modeling by access pattern.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Embed when data is read together and bounded in size; split when growth or independent querying becomes significant.

contents.title: Accelerating Systems with Redis Caching
contents.description: Learn how to integrate Redis into NestJS and apply caching at three layers: response layer, logic layer, and database query layer to reduce database load and improve response speed.
contents.body:
## I. Introduction

Both **PostgreSQL** and **MongoDB** persist data on disk (SSD/HDD). Even with indexing and optimized queries, complex operations still involve disk I/O, which is much slower than RAM.

Imagine **one million** concurrent users requesting the same leaderboard. If every request recomputes the result from scratch, the database becomes overloaded quickly. The practical solution is to introduce a **cache layer** between the application and database so frequently requested data does not need to be recomputed on every call.

## II. Essence

This lesson follows a **source-first** approach: read the code that applies cache at three layers, then call the same APIs repeatedly to observe cache misses, cache hits, and how Redis relieves PostgreSQL pressure.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis)

### Runtime Dependency Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> CatsController[CatsController]
    CatsController --> RespCache[CacheInterceptor - response layer]
    CatsController --> CatsService[CatsService]
    CatsService --> LogicCache[CACHE_MANAGER - logic layer]
    CatsService --> TypeOrmCache[TypeORM query cache - db layer]
    LogicCache --> Redis[(Redis)]
    TypeOrmCache --> Redis
    CatsService --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
```

### Source Code Tree (file-level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "app.module.ts"
        "modules"
            "cats"
                "cats.module.ts"
                "cats.controller.ts"
                "cats.service.ts"
                "entities/cat.entity.ts"
        "infrastructure"
            "cache/cache.module.ts"
            "database/typeorm.config.ts"
```

### Environment Setup and Run Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop, and Git are required.
- **2. Clone the demo source:** Clone/pull the source for consistent context:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Start PostgreSQL and Redis:** Run both data infrastructure services:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f .docker/postgresql.yaml up -d
  docker compose -f .docker/redis.yaml up -d
  ```
- **4. Install dependencies and run the app:** Install packages and start the server:
  ```bash
  npm install --legacy-peer-deps
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** The app runs on port `3000`; repeated requests to the same endpoint become noticeably faster.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Test response-layer caching by calling the same endpoint repeatedly.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - response layer cache - GET http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `GET http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer` twice in a row.

  **Body JSON:** No request body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer
  ```

- **Step 2:** Test logic-layer and db-layer caching to compare control granularity.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - logic and db layer cache - GET http://localhost:3000/cats/logic-layer + GET http://localhost:3000/cats/db-layer**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to call `GET /cats/logic-layer` and `GET /cats/db-layer`; call each endpoint twice.

  **Body JSON:** No request body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/logic-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/logic-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/db-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/db-layer
  ```

  **Trace code execution (by file):**
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:18`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L18) -> `CatsController.getResponseLayerCached()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:27`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L27) -> `CatsController.getLogicLayerCached()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:22`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L22) -> `CatsService.findWithLogicCache()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:48`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L48) -> `CatsService.findWithDatabaseCache()`
  - [`src/infrastructure/database/typeorm.config.ts:15`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/infrastructure/database/typeorm.config.ts#L15) -> query cache configuration

  *Expected result:* The first call is a cache miss and hits the DB; subsequent calls are cache hits and return faster.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Response-layer Caching***

- **Role:** Cache the entire controller response for fast rollout on read-heavy endpoints.
- **Common mistake:** Applying cache to highly volatile data without shortening TTL.
- **Production impact:** Users receive stale data for too long.

### 2. ***Logic-layer Caching***

- **Role:** Use `CACHE_MANAGER` for fine-grained key/TTL/invalidation control tied to business rules.
- **Common mistake:** Poor key namespacing that causes cache collisions across contexts.
- **Production impact:** Wrong data returned for specific users/tenants.

### 3. ***Database Query Caching***

- **Role:** TypeORM cache reduces repeated expensive queries without major business-code changes.
- **Common mistake:** Enabling query cache for strictly real-time transactional data.
- **Production impact:** Reports and metrics drift from freshly written records.

### 4. ***Cache Invalidation***

- **Role:** TTL or event-driven invalidation balances speed and freshness.
- **Common mistake:** Adding cache without a clear invalidation strategy.
- **Production impact:** Business bugs caused by prolonged stale data.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

In production, define a layered cache strategy instead of a one-size-fits-all TTL. Use short TTLs at response layer, explicit key invalidation at logic layer, and carefully scoped query cache at database layer. Track cache hit ratio, memory pressure, and stale-data incidents to continuously tune behavior.

**Conclusion:** Caching is not just "adding Redis"; it is deciding what to cache, where to cache it, and when to invalidate it safely.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   "Would you choose response-layer or logic-layer cache for a leaderboard that updates every 5 minutes?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to choose cache layer based on data volatility and control needs.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Start with short-TTL response-layer cache; move to logic-layer cache if event-driven invalidation is needed.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   "What signals indicate your cache is hurting the system instead of helping?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Operational observation skills for stale/inconsistent data.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Mention DB mismatch, low hit ratio, key explosion, memory pressure, and invalidation failures.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   "How would you design cache keys for a multi-tenant system to prevent data leaks?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Safe namespace/key strategy design.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Include tenant/user scope in keys, use versioned prefixes, define TTL policy, and support tenant-scoped invalidation.

translations.value: Tăng tốc hệ thống với bộ nhớ đệm Redis
Tìm hiểu cách tích hợp Redis vào NestJS để caching dữ liệu ở 3 tầng khác nhau: Response layer, Logic layer và Database Query layer, từ đó giảm tải cho database và tăng tốc độ phản hồi.

## I. Lời mở đầu

Cả **PostgreSQL** lẫn **MongoDB** đều lưu trữ dữ liệu trên ổ cứng (SSD/HDD). Dù đã tối ưu bằng indexing hay aggregation, mọi truy vấn phức tạp vẫn phải thực hiện thao tác **I/O ổ cứng** — với tốc độ chậm hơn RAM hàng trăm lần.

Hãy tưởng tượng có **1 triệu** người dùng đồng thời truy cập để xem bảng xếp hạng "Top 10 Phim hay nhất". Nếu mọi request đều buộc database tính toán lại từ đầu — quét bảng, **GROUP BY**, sắp xếp — server sẽ quá tải và sụp đổ trong vài phút. Giải pháp là đặt một lớp **bộ nhớ đệm (Cache)** giữa ứng dụng và database, để những dữ liệu được truy vấn thường xuyên không cần phải tính toán lại mỗi lần.

## II. Bản chất

Bài này đi theo hướng **source-first**: đọc code áp dụng cache ở 3 tầng trước, rồi gọi API lặp lại để thấy rõ cache miss/hit và cách Redis giảm tải cho PostgreSQL.

```mermaid
    CatsService --> TypeOrmCache[TypeORM query cache - db layer]
```


### Chuẩn bị Môi trường và Luồng Cài đặt

- **1. Prerequisites:** Cần `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop và git.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source để đọc đúng context code:

### Kiểm thử ứng dụng

  **Tiêu đề API:** **Cats API - response layer cache - GET http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer**

  **Hướng dẫn gọi API:** Dùng Postman gửi `GET` tới `http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer` hai lần liên tiếp.

- **Bước 2:** Test logic-layer và db-layer cache để so sánh mức độ kiểm soát.

  **Hướng dẫn gọi API:** Dùng Postman gọi lần lượt `GET /cats/logic-layer` và `GET /cats/db-layer`, mỗi endpoint gọi 2 lần.

  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:27`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L27) -> `CatsController.getLogicLayerCached()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:22`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L22) -> `CatsService.findWithLogicCache()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:48`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L48) -> `CatsService.findWithDatabaseCache()`

  *Kết luận:* Redis giúp hạ áp lực database, nhưng cần chiến lược invalidation để tránh stale data.

## III. Các khái niệm cốt lõi

### 1. ***Response-layer caching***

- **Vai trò:** Cache toàn bộ response ở tầng controller, triển khai nhanh cho endpoint read-heavy.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Áp cache cho endpoint dữ liệu biến động cao mà không giảm TTL.
- **Hậu quả production:** Người dùng nhận stale data quá lâu.

### 2. ***Logic-layer caching***

- **Vai trò:** Dùng `CACHE_MANAGER` để kiểm soát key/TTL/invalidation chi tiết theo nghiệp vụ.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Đặt key không có namespace rõ ràng dẫn tới đè cache giữa các context.
- **Hậu quả production:** Trả sai dữ liệu theo user/tenant.

### 3. ***Database query caching***

- **Vai trò:** TypeORM cache giảm tải query lặp nặng mà không đổi nhiều business code.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Bật cache query cho dữ liệu transactional cần realtime tuyệt đối.
- **Hậu quả production:** Báo cáo/metrics lệch so với dữ liệu mới ghi.

### 4. ***Cache invalidation***

- **Vai trò:** TTL hoặc event-driven invalidation giúp cân bằng tốc độ và độ tươi dữ liệu.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Chỉ cache mà không có chiến lược xóa cache khi dữ liệu đổi.
- **Hậu quả production:** Tăng bug nghiệp vụ do dữ liệu cũ kéo dài.

## IV. Kết luận

**Redis** là công cụ không thể thiếu trong kiến trúc Backend hiện đại. Với 3 tầng caching — **Response**, **Logic** và **Database Query** — NestJS mang lại sự linh hoạt tối đa trong việc lựa chọn chiến lược cache phù hợp với từng trường hợp sử dụng cụ thể.

**Kết luận:** Caching không chỉ là "thêm Redis vào hệ thống" — mà là hiểu rõ dữ liệu nào cần cache, cache ở tầng nào, và khi nào cần vô hiệu hóa cache để đảm bảo người dùng luôn nhận được dữ liệu chính xác.

## V. Các mẫu câu phỏng vấn

1. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Bạn chọn response-layer hay logic-layer cache cho endpoint bảng xếp hạng cập nhật mỗi 5 phút?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Năng lực chọn tầng cache theo tốc độ thay đổi dữ liệu và độ linh hoạt nghiệp vụ.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Có thể bắt đầu response-layer với TTL ngắn; chuyển logic-layer nếu cần invalidation chủ động theo sự kiện.

2. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Dấu hiệu nào cho thấy cache đang gây hại thay vì giúp hệ thống?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Tư duy quan sát hệ thống và phát hiện stale/inconsistent data.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Nêu các dấu hiệu như dữ liệu lệch DB, hit ratio thấp, key bùng nổ, memory pressure, invalidation thất bại.

3. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Bạn thiết kế cache key thế nào cho hệ thống multi-tenant để không leak dữ liệu?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Khả năng thiết kế namespace/key strategy an toàn.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Thêm tenantId/user scope vào key, chuẩn prefix version, kiểm soát TTL và xóa key theo tenant khi có cập nhật lớn.
Accelerating Systems with Redis Caching
Learn how to integrate Redis into NestJS and apply caching at three layers: response layer, logic layer, and database query layer to reduce database load and improve response speed.

## I. Introduction

Both **PostgreSQL** and **MongoDB** persist data on disk (SSD/HDD). Even with indexing and optimized queries, complex operations still involve disk I/O, which is much slower than RAM.

Imagine **one million** concurrent users requesting the same leaderboard. If every request recomputes the result from scratch, the database becomes overloaded quickly. The practical solution is to introduce a **cache layer** between the application and database so frequently requested data does not need to be recomputed on every call.

## II. Essence

This lesson follows a **source-first** approach: read the code that applies cache at three layers, then call the same APIs repeatedly to observe cache misses, cache hits, and how Redis relieves PostgreSQL pressure.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis)

### Runtime Dependency Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> CatsController[CatsController]
    CatsController --> RespCache[CacheInterceptor - response layer]
    CatsController --> CatsService[CatsService]
    CatsService --> LogicCache[CACHE_MANAGER - logic layer]
    CatsService --> TypeOrmCache[TypeORM query cache - db layer]
    LogicCache --> Redis[(Redis)]
    TypeOrmCache --> Redis
    CatsService --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
```

```mermaid
treeView-beta

        "app.module.ts"

                "entities/cat.entity.ts"
        "infrastructure"

```

### Environment Setup and Run Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop, and Git are required.
- **2. Clone the demo source:** Clone/pull the source for consistent context:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Start PostgreSQL and Redis:** Run both data infrastructure services:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f .docker/postgresql.yaml up -d
  docker compose -f .docker/redis.yaml up -d
  ```
- **4. Install dependencies and run the app:** Install packages and start the server:
  ```bash
  npm install --legacy-peer-deps
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** The app runs on port `3000`; repeated requests to the same endpoint become noticeably faster.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Test response-layer caching by calling the same endpoint repeatedly.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - response layer cache - GET http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `GET http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer` twice in a row.

  **Body JSON:** No request body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer
  ```

- **Step 2:** Test logic-layer and db-layer caching to compare control granularity.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - logic and db layer cache - GET http://localhost:3000/cats/logic-layer + GET http://localhost:3000/cats/db-layer**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to call `GET /cats/logic-layer` and `GET /cats/db-layer`; call each endpoint twice.

  **Body JSON:** No request body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/logic-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/logic-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/db-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/db-layer
  ```

  **Trace code execution (by file):**
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:18`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L18) -> `CatsController.getResponseLayerCached()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:27`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L27) -> `CatsController.getLogicLayerCached()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:22`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L22) -> `CatsService.findWithLogicCache()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:48`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L48) -> `CatsService.findWithDatabaseCache()`
  - [`src/infrastructure/database/typeorm.config.ts:15`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/infrastructure/database/typeorm.config.ts#L15) -> query cache configuration

  *Expected result:* The first call is a cache miss and hits the DB; subsequent calls are cache hits and return faster.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Response-layer Caching***

- **Role:** Cache the entire controller response for fast rollout on read-heavy endpoints.
- **Common mistake:** Applying cache to highly volatile data without shortening TTL.
- **Production impact:** Users receive stale data for too long.

### 2. ***Logic-layer Caching***

- **Role:** Use `CACHE_MANAGER` for fine-grained key/TTL/invalidation control tied to business rules.
- **Common mistake:** Poor key namespacing that causes cache collisions across contexts.
- **Production impact:** Wrong data returned for specific users/tenants.

### 3. ***Database Query Caching***

- **Role:** TypeORM cache reduces repeated expensive queries without major business-code changes.
- **Common mistake:** Enabling query cache for strictly real-time transactional data.
- **Production impact:** Reports and metrics drift from freshly written records.

### 4. ***Cache Invalidation***

- **Role:** TTL or event-driven invalidation balances speed and freshness.
- **Common mistake:** Adding cache without a clear invalidation strategy.
- **Production impact:** Business bugs caused by prolonged stale data.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

In production, define a layered cache strategy instead of a one-size-fits-all TTL. Use short TTLs at response layer, explicit key invalidation at logic layer, and carefully scoped query cache at database layer. Track cache hit ratio, memory pressure, and stale-data incidents to continuously tune behavior.

**Conclusion:** Caching is not just "adding Redis"; it is deciding what to cache, where to cache it, and when to invalidate it safely.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   "Would you choose response-layer or logic-layer cache for a leaderboard that updates every 5 minutes?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to choose cache layer based on data volatility and control needs.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Start with short-TTL response-layer cache; move to logic-layer cache if event-driven invalidation is needed.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   "What signals indicate your cache is hurting the system instead of helping?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Operational observation skills for stale/inconsistent data.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Mention DB mismatch, low hit ratio, key explosion, memory pressure, and invalidation failures.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   "How would you design cache keys for a multi-tenant system to prevent data leaks?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Safe namespace/key strategy design.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Include tenant/user scope in keys, use versioned prefixes, define TTL policy, and support tenant-scoped invalidation.

steps.title: Implement all CRUD endpoints
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: In `TasksService`, implement the following methods:
    - `create(data)`: add a new task to the array, return the created task.
    - `findAll()`: return the entire task array.
    - `findOne(id)`: find a task by id, throw `NotFoundException` if not found.
    - `update(id, data)`: update a task by id, throw `NotFoundException` if not found.
    - `remove(id)`: delete a task by id, throw `NotFoundException` if not found.
  - Step 2: In `TasksController`, create endpoints with correct HTTP methods and status codes:
    - `@Post()` for `POST /tasks` with `@HttpCode(HttpStatus.CREATED)` -> calls `create()`.
    - `@Get()` for `GET /tasks` -> calls `findAll()`.
    - `@Get(':id')` for `GET /tasks/:id` -> calls `findOne()`.
    - `@Patch(':id')` for `PATCH /tasks/:id` -> calls `update()`.
    - `@Delete(':id')` for `DELETE /tasks/:id` with `@HttpCode(HttpStatus.NO_CONTENT)` -> calls `remove()`.
  - Step 3: Ensure URLs use plural nouns (`/tasks`), no verbs like `/createTask` or `/deleteTask`.
- **Expected result:** All 5 endpoints work correctly with the appropriate HTTP methods and status codes.
- **Conclusion:** The REST API follows RESTful conventions for naming and HTTP semantics.

steps.title: Create CreateTaskDto with class-validator decorators
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create file `create-task.dto.ts` in the `tasks/dto/` directory.
  - Step 2: Declare class `CreateTaskDto` with fields and decorators:
    - `title`: apply `@IsString()` and `@MinLength(3)`.
    - `description`: apply `@IsString()` and `@IsOptional()`.
    - `priority`: apply `@IsEnum(['low', 'medium', 'high'])`.
  - Step 3: In `TasksController`, change the body parameter type from `any` to `CreateTaskDto`:
    ```typescript
    @Post()
    create(@Body() createTaskDto: CreateTaskDto) { ... }
    ```
  - Step 4: Enable `ValidationPipe` globally in `main.ts`:
    ```typescript
    app.useGlobalPipes(new ValidationPipe({
      whitelist: true,
      forbidNonWhitelisted: true,
    }));
    ```
- **Expected result:** `POST /tasks` with a body missing `title` or `title` shorter than 3 characters returns 400 Bad Request with a specific error message.
- **Conclusion:** DTO and ValidationPipe now protect the endpoint from invalid data.

steps.title: Test validation and whitelist behavior
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Start the application:
    ```bash
    npm run start:dev
    ```
  - Step 2: Send a valid request:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/tasks -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"title\":\"Fix bug\",\"priority\":\"high\"}"
    ```
    Verify it returns 201 with the created task.
  - Step 3: Send a request missing `title`:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/tasks -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"priority\":\"low\"}"
    ```
    Verify it returns 400 Bad Request with a message indicating `title` is required.
  - Step 4: Send a request with `title` too short:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/tasks -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"title\":\"AB\",\"priority\":\"low\"}"
    ```
    Verify it returns 400 with a message indicating `title` must have at least 3 characters.
  - Step 5: Send a request with an unknown field `role`:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/tasks -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"title\":\"Fix bug\",\"priority\":\"high\",\"role\":\"admin\"}"
    ```
    Verify it returns 400 with a message indicating `role` is not allowed (`forbidNonWhitelisted`).
  - Step 6: Send a request with invalid `priority` value:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/tasks -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"title\":\"Fix bug\",\"priority\":\"urgent\"}"
    ```
    Verify it returns 400 with a message indicating `priority` must be a valid enum value.
- **Expected result:**
  - Valid body -> 201 Created.
  - Missing `title` -> 400 Bad Request.
  - `title` < 3 characters -> 400 Bad Request.
  - Unknown field `role` -> 400 Bad Request (forbidNonWhitelisted).
  - Invalid `priority` enum -> 400 Bad Request.
- **Conclusion:** If all cases return the correct status code and appropriate error messages, DTO and ValidationPipe are working correctly.

    Xác nhận trả về 400 Bad Request với message chỉ rõ `title` là bắt buộc.
  - Bước 4: Gửi request với `title` quá ngắn:

steps.title: Build the TransformInterceptor
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create file `transform.interceptor.ts` in the `common/interceptors/` directory.
  - Step 2: Implement class `TransformInterceptor` implementing `NestInterceptor`. In the `intercept()` method, use `pipe(map(data => ...))` to wrap the response into:
    ```typescript
    {
      statusCode: context.switchToHttp().getResponse().statusCode,
      message: 'Success',
      data: data,
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    }
    ```
  - Step 3: Register it globally in `main.ts`:
    ```typescript
    app.useGlobalInterceptors(new TransformInterceptor());
    ```
- **Expected result:** Every successful response has the structure `{ statusCode, message, data, timestamp }`.
- **Conclusion:** TransformInterceptor has standardized the response format for success cases.

steps.title: Build the AllExceptionsFilter
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create file `all-exceptions.filter.ts` in the `common/filters/` directory.
  - Step 2: Implement class `AllExceptionsFilter` implementing `ExceptionFilter` with the `@Catch()` decorator (no parameters to catch all exception types).
  - Step 3: In the `catch(exception, host)` method:
    - If `exception` is an `HttpException`, extract `statusCode` and `message` from the exception.
    - If not an `HttpException`, return `statusCode: 500` and `message: 'Internal Server Error'`.
    - Return a JSON response in the format:
      ```typescript
      {
        statusCode: status,
        error: HttpStatus[status] || 'Internal Server Error',
        message: message,
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
      }
      ```
    - Never expose the `stack trace` externally.
  - Step 4: Register it globally in `main.ts`:
    ```typescript
    app.useGlobalFilters(new AllExceptionsFilter());
    ```
- **Expected result:** Every exception returns safe JSON with a unified structure, no stack traces leaked.
- **Conclusion:** AllExceptionsFilter protects the application from leaking sensitive information through error responses.

translations.value: Xây dựng AllExceptionsFilter

- **Các bước thực hiện:**
  - Bước 1: Tạo file `all-exceptions.filter.ts` trong thư mục `common/filters/`.
  - Bước 2: Implement class `AllExceptionsFilter` implement `ExceptionFilter` với decorator `@Catch()` (không truyền tham số để bắt mọi loại exception).
  - Bước 3: Trong hàm `catch(exception, host)`:
    - Nếu `exception` là `HttpException`, lấy `statusCode` và `message` từ exception.
    - Nếu không phải `HttpException`, trả `statusCode: 500` và `message: 'Internal Server Error'`.
    - Trả response JSON dạng:
      ```typescript
      {
        statusCode: status,
        error: HttpStatus[status] || 'Internal Server Error',
        message: message,
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
      }
      ```
    - Không bao giờ trả `stack trace` ra ngoài.
  - Bước 4: Đăng ký toàn cục trong `main.ts`:
    ```typescript
    app.useGlobalFilters(new AllExceptionsFilter());
    ```
- **Kết quả mong đợi:** Mọi exception đều trả JSON an toàn với cấu trúc thống nhất, không lộ stack trace.
- **Kết luận:** AllExceptionsFilter đã bảo vệ ứng dụng khỏi việc lộ thông tin nhạy cảm qua error response.

steps.title: Test the unified response format
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Start the application:
    ```bash
    npm run start:dev
    ```
  - Step 2: Call a successful endpoint:
    ```bash
    curl http://localhost:3000/tasks
    ```
    Verify the response has the format:
    ```json
    {
      "statusCode": 200,
      "message": "Success",
      "data": [...],
      "timestamp": "2025-..."
    }
    ```
  - Step 3: Call an endpoint with a non-existent id (NotFoundException):
    ```bash
    curl http://localhost:3000/tasks/999
    ```
    Verify the response has the format:
    ```json
    {
      "statusCode": 404,
      "error": "Not Found",
      "message": "...",
      "timestamp": "2025-..."
    }
    ```
  - Step 4: Create a temporary endpoint `GET /tasks/crash` in the controller that throws `new Error('Unexpected')` (non-HttpException error). Call this endpoint:
    ```bash
    curl http://localhost:3000/tasks/crash
    ```
    Verify the response returns 500 with safe JSON, no stack trace included.
- **Expected result:**
  - `GET /tasks` -> `{ statusCode: 200, message: "Success", data: [...], timestamp }`.
  - `GET /tasks/999` -> `{ statusCode: 404, error: "Not Found", message, timestamp }`.
  - `GET /tasks/crash` -> `{ statusCode: 500, error: "Internal Server Error", message, timestamp }` with no stack trace.
- **Conclusion:** If all responses (both success and error) have a unified JSON structure and do not leak sensitive information, the system meets the requirements.

steps.title: Configure Swagger in main.ts
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: In `main.ts`, import `SwaggerModule` and `DocumentBuilder` from `@nestjs/swagger`.
  - Step 2: Create the Swagger configuration using `DocumentBuilder`:
    ```typescript
    const config = new DocumentBuilder()
      .setTitle('Task Management API')
      .setDescription('Auto-generated API documentation for Task management')
      .setVersion('1.0')
      .addBearerAuth()
      .build();
    ```
  - Step 3: Create the document and mount Swagger UI:
    ```typescript
    const document = SwaggerModule.createDocument(app, config);
    SwaggerModule.setup('docs', app, document);
    ```
  - Step 4: Start the application and navigate to `http://localhost:3000/docs` in the browser.
- **Expected result:** Swagger UI is displayed at `/docs` with the title, description, and an Authorize button for Bearer token.
- **Conclusion:** Swagger has been successfully integrated, ready to attach decorators to controllers and DTOs.

    - Confirm `POST /tasks` has a request body schema with examples from `@ApiProperty`.

Viết tài liệu API với Swagger OpenAPI
Cấu hình tự động sinh tài liệu API sống, tương tác trực quan bằng Swagger và Scalar ngay từ trong code NestJS, thay thế hoàn toàn cách viết tài liệu thủ công.

## I. Lời mở đầu

Viết xong ***API*** mà không có tài liệu đi kèm thì đội ngũ **Frontend** và **Mobile** sẽ không biết gọi đường dẫn nào, truyền tham số gì, hay kỳ vọng response như thế nào. Cách truyền thống như chia sẻ file **Postman** hay viết **Excel** thường nhanh chóng bị lỗi thời khi code thay đổi. ***Swagger*** (tiêu chuẩn ***OpenAPI***) giải quyết vấn đề này bằng cách đọc trực tiếp code và tự động tạo ra một trang tài liệu web **sống**, luôn đồng bộ với trạng thái hiện tại của ***API***.

## II. Bản chất

Bài này đi theo hướng **code-first**: đọc cấu hình ***Swagger***/***OpenAPI*** từ source trước, sau đó test tài liệu ***API*** sống để xác nhận endpoint, schema và response luôn đồng bộ với code.

Clone tại [đây](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/swagger-api-documentation)

### 1. Giá trị của tài liệu API sống

Tài liệu ***API*** truyền thống (Word, Excel, Postman collection) có một điểm yếu chí mạng: chúng bị **lỗi thời** ngay khi developer sửa code mà quên cập nhật file. ***Swagger*** loại bỏ vấn đề này bằng cách sinh tài liệu tự động từ chính source code, đảm bảo tài liệu luôn phản ánh đúng các endpoint, tham số, và response đang hoạt động.

- **Ví dụ:** Khi bạn thêm một trường mới vào ***DTO*** và gắn `@ApiProperty()`, giao diện ***Swagger*** tự động hiển thị trường đó trong phần request body mà không cần chỉnh sửa bất kỳ file tài liệu nào.

### 2. Cấu hình Swagger trong main.ts

Để kích hoạt ***Swagger***, bạn cài thư viện `@nestjs/swagger` và cấu hình trong file `main.ts` trước khi gọi `app.listen()`.

- **Ví dụ:** Cấu hình cơ bản:

```typescript
const config = new DocumentBuilder()
  .setTitle('StarCi Academy Backend')
  .setDescription('API documentation')
  .setVersion('1.0')
  .addBearerAuth()
  .build();

const document = SwaggerModule.createDocument(app, config);
SwaggerModule.setup('swagger', app, document);
```

Sau khi cấu hình, truy cập `http://localhost:3000/swagger` để xem giao diện tài liệu ***Swagger*** classic. Dự án này cũng tích hợp ***Scalar*** tại đường dẫn `/scalar` với giao diện hiện đại hơn.

### 3. Swagger Decorators

Để giao diện tài liệu thêm chi tiết và hữu ích, bạn sử dụng các **decorator** của ***Swagger*** trong ***Controller***. Mỗi decorator bổ sung thông tin mô tả cho từng endpoint, giúp Frontend hiểu rõ chức năng mà không cần đọc code.

- **Ví dụ:** Sử dụng decorator trong ***Controller***:

```typescript
@ApiTags('Cats Module')
@Controller('cats')
export class CatsController {

  @Get()
  @ApiOperation({ summary: 'Retrieve all cats' })
  @ApiResponse({ status: 200, description: 'List of cats returned successfully' })
  findAll() { return this.catsService.findAll(); }

  @Post()
  @ApiOperation({ summary: 'Create a new cat' })
  @ApiResponse({ status: 201, description: 'Cat created successfully' })
  @ApiResponse({ status: 400, description: 'Invalid payload' })
  create(@Body() dto: CreateCatDto) { return this.catsService.create(dto); }
}
```

### 4. Hiển thị DTO với @ApiProperty()

**TypeScript** bị xóa cấu trúc kiểu khi build ra **JavaScript**, nên ***Swagger*** không thể tự động nhận biết các trường bên trong ***DTO***. Bạn phải sử dụng `@ApiProperty()` để khai báo từng thuộc tính, giúp ***Swagger*** hiển thị đầy đủ thông tin và tạo sẵn mock data trên giao diện.

- **Ví dụ:** Khai báo ***DTO*** với ***ApiProperty***:

```typescript
export class CreateCatDto {
  @ApiProperty({ example: 'Persian', description: 'Breed of the cat' })
  @IsString()
  breed: string;

  @ApiProperty({ example: 2, description: 'Age in years' })
  @IsNumber()
  age: number;
}
```

Trên giao diện ***Swagger***, trường `breed` và `age` sẽ hiển thị đầy đủ với dữ liệu mẫu, cho phép Frontend thử nghiệm trực tiếp mà không cần tự điền dữ liệu.

### Chuẩn bị Môi trường và Luồng Cài đặt

- **1. Prerequisites:** Cần `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, git.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source để đọc đúng context code:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/swagger-api-documentation
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Cài dependency:** Cài package tại thư mục project:
  ```bash
  npm install
  ```
- **4. Lệnh khởi chạy:** Chạy app local:
  ```bash
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Tín hiệu thành công:** Truy cập được `/swagger` và `/scalar`, endpoint hiển thị đầy đủ.

### Kiểm thử ứng dụng

Phần test dưới đây bám trên lần chạy source thật (`npm run start:dev`) và gọi ***API*** thật.

- **Bước 1:** Kiểm tra docs endpoint có hoạt động (***Swagger***/***Scalar***).

  **Tiêu đề API:**  
  **Docs API — mở giao diện Swagger — GET http://localhost:55002/swagger:**

  **Body JSON:** Không có body với request `GET`.

  Hoặc dùng **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:55002/swagger
  ```

  *Kết quả mong đợi:* Trả `200 OK`, UI docs hiển thị đầy đủ endpoint và schema.

  **Response mẫu (thực tế):**
  ```json
  {
    "statusCode": 200,
    "note": "Swagger HTML trả về, content-length quan sát được là 3144 bytes"
  }
  ```

  *Kết luận:* ***OpenAPI*** document được build từ code và publish thành công lên cả ***Swagger UI*** và ***Scalar UI***.

  **Trace code execution (kèm link source):**
  - [`src/main.ts:29`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/swagger-api-documentation/src/main.ts#L29) -> `SwaggerModule.createDocument(app, config)`
  - [`src/main.ts:44`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/swagger-api-documentation/src/main.ts#L44) -> `SwaggerModule.setup('swagger', app, document)`

  ```ts
  // Phase 1 - Sinh OpenAPI document từ code và mount UI
  // src/main.ts
  const document = SwaggerModule.createDocument(app, config);
  app.use('/scalar', apiReference({ spec: { content: document } } as any));
  SwaggerModule.setup('swagger', app, document);
  ```

- **Bước 2:** Gọi endpoint business từ docs để xác nhận contract success.

  **Tiêu đề API:**  
  **Cats API — đọc danh sách mèo — GET http://localhost:55002/cats:**

  **Hướng dẫn gọi API:** Dùng nút **Try it out** trong ***Swagger***/***Scalar*** với `GET /cats` hoặc gọi curl trực tiếp.

  ```json
    "data": [
      {
        "name": "Milo",
  ```

  **Trace code execution (kèm link source):**
  - [`src/modules/cat/cat.controller.ts:14`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/swagger-api-documentation/src/modules/cat/cat.controller.ts#L14) -> `CatController.findAll()`
  - [`src/modules/cat/cat.controller.ts:16`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/swagger-api-documentation/src/modules/cat/cat.controller.ts#L16) -> `@ApiOperation(...)`
  - [`src/common/interceptors/transform.interceptor.ts:32`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/swagger-api-documentation/src/common/interceptors/transform.interceptor.ts#L32) -> bọc response chuẩn

  ```ts
  // Phase 1 - Controller khai báo endpoint với Swagger decorator
  // src/modules/cat/cat.controller.ts
  @Get()
  @ResponseMessage('Lấy danh sách mèo thành công (EN: Get all cats success)')
  @ApiOperation({ summary: 'Lấy tất cả mèo' })
  findAll() {
    return [{ name: 'Milo', age: 3 }];
  ```

- **Bước 3:** Test failure path để kiểm chứng docs + error contract.

  **Tiêu đề API:**  
  **Cats API — demo lỗi có chuẩn JSON — GET http://localhost:55002/cats/error-demo:**

  **Trace code execution (kèm link source):**
  - [`src/modules/cat/cat.controller.ts:29`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/swagger-api-documentation/src/modules/cat/cat.controller.ts#L29) -> `CatController.triggerError()`

**Kết luận kiểm thử:** ***Swagger***/***Scalar*** docs và runtime hiện đồng bộ: endpoint hiển thị đúng, success response đúng contract, và failure response cũng chuẩn hóa nhất quán.

## III. Các khái niệm cốt lõi

### 1. ***OpenAPI as Source of Truth***

- **Vai trò:** Dùng tài liệu sinh từ code làm contract chính thức giữa backend và client.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Duy trì docs thủ công tách rời codebase.
- **Hệ quả production:** Docs lệch runtime, QA/frontend test sai endpoint hoặc payload.

### 2. ***DocumentBuilder & Global Setup***

- **Vai trò:** Chuẩn hóa title/version/auth scheme cho toàn ***API*** tại `main.ts`.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Cấu hình ***Swagger*** rời rạc từng module.
- **Hệ quả production:** Tài liệu thiếu nhất quán, khó onboard team mới.

### 3. ***Decorator-driven Endpoint Metadata***

- **Vai trò:** `@ApiOperation`, `@ApiResponse`, `@ApiTags` mô tả endpoint ngay tại nơi định nghĩa route.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Bỏ trống response schema/status quan trọng.
- **Hệ quả production:** Consumer không biết rõ contract success/error của endpoint.

### 4. ***DTO Schema Exposure***

- **Vai trò:** `@ApiProperty` giúp hiển thị field/type/example chính xác.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** ***DTO*** có validate nhưng không có metadata docs.
- **Hệ quả production:** Tài liệu body thiếu field hoặc không rõ format dữ liệu.

## IV. Kỹ thuật nâng cao

Với hệ thống lớn, tài liệu ***API*** nên được dùng trực tiếp trong CI/CD: validate ***OpenAPI*** spec, phát hiện breaking change, và đồng bộ auto-generated client SDK cho frontend/mobile. Khi kết hợp versioning và deprecation policy rõ ràng, đội kỹ thuật có thể phát hành ***API*** nhanh mà vẫn an toàn cho consumer hiện tại.

**Kết luận:** ***Swagger***/***OpenAPI*** không chỉ là giao diện xem endpoint, mà là hạ tầng quản trị vòng đời ***API***.

## V. Các mẫu câu phỏng vấn

1. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   "Vì sao tài liệu ***API*** thủ công dễ gây incident khi hệ thống phát triển nhanh?"
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Hiểu rủi ro contract drift giữa docs và runtime.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Code thay đổi liên tục làm docs cũ nhanh; client gọi sai payload/endpoint dẫn tới lỗi tích hợp.

2. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   "`@ApiProperty` giải quyết vấn đề gì mà TypeScript type đơn thuần không giải quyết được?"
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Nắm cơ chế metadata runtime và ***OpenAPI*** generation.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** TS type bị erase khi build; `@ApiProperty` cung cấp metadata runtime để ***Swagger*** dựng schema.

3. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   "Bạn làm gì để phát hiện breaking change ***API*** trước khi deploy?"
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Tư duy DevEx + CI cho ***API*** lifecycle.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Diff ***OpenAPI*** spec trong CI, enforce versioning/deprecation, chạy contract tests với consumer chính.

steps.title: Initialize the project and configure PostgreSQL with Docker
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create a new project using the CLI:
    ```bash
    nest new jwt-authentication-flow-easy
    ```
  - Step 2: Navigate to the project directory and install required dependencies:
    ```bash
    cd jwt-authentication-flow-easy
    npm install @nestjs/typeorm typeorm pg @nestjs/jwt @nestjs/passport passport passport-jwt bcrypt
    npm install -D @types/passport-jwt @types/bcrypt
    ```
  - Step 3: Create a `docker-compose.yml` file at the project root with PostgreSQL:
    ```yaml
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        ports:
          - "5432:5432"
        environment:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: jwt_auth_db
    ```
  - Step 4: Start PostgreSQL:
    ```bash
    docker compose up -d
    ```
  - Step 5: Configure `TypeOrmModule.forRoot()` in `AppModule` with PostgreSQL connection details, enable `synchronize: true` to auto-create tables from entities.
- **Expected result:** PostgreSQL runs on port 5432, the NestJS application connects successfully and is ready to create tables from entities.
- **Conclusion:** The project environment and database are ready for implementing the authentication module.
