contents.title: Complex Applications and Helm Charts
contents.description: Deploy three production-style database clusters on Kubernetes with Helm: MongoDB Sharded, PostgreSQL HA, and Redis Cluster - using Bitnami OCI charts and practical high-availability configuration.
contents.body:
## I. Introduction

Running a single MySQL Pod and a small NestJS Deployment is enough for demos, but senior-level interviews quickly move to real operations:
- How do you run MongoDB with replica sets and sharding?
- How fast is PostgreSQL failover from primary to standby?
- How do you deploy Redis Cluster with slot distribution and replication?

Hand-writing all Kubernetes manifests for stateful database clusters is slow and error-prone. Common mistakes include unstable hostnames between replicas or missing `volumeClaimTemplates`, which can lead to data loss.

This is exactly why teams use ***Helm***. Like `npm` for Node.js, Helm packages many Kubernetes manifests into reusable ***Charts*** with configurable ***Values***. With one `helm install`, you can deploy proven architecture patterns maintained by the community.

## II. Essence

We deploy three clusters inside namespace `database` (Minikube or DOKS):
- ***MongoDB Sharded*** (11 Pods): 2 shards x 3 data nodes + 3 config servers + 2 mongos routers  
  Endpoint: `mongodb-sharded-mongodb-sharded.database.svc.cluster.local:27017`
- ***PostgreSQL HA*** (5 Pods): 3 repmgr PostgreSQL nodes (1 primary + 2 standby) + 2 pgpool  
  Endpoint: `postgresql-ha-pgpool.database.svc.cluster.local:5432`
- ***Redis Cluster*** (6 Pods): 3 master + 3 replica nodes  
  Endpoint: `redis-cluster.database.svc.cluster.local:6379`

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/system-design-mastery/complex-applications-and-helm-charts)

| Cluster | OCI Chart | Components | Total Pods | In-cluster Endpoint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **MongoDB Sharded** | `bitnamicharts/mongodb-sharded` | 2 shards x 3 data nodes + 3 config servers + 2 mongos | **11** | `mongodb-sharded-mongodb-sharded.database.svc.cluster.local:27017` |
| **PostgreSQL HA** | `bitnamicharts/postgresql-ha` | 3 `postgresql-repmgr` + 2 pgpool | **5** | `postgresql-ha-pgpool.database.svc.cluster.local:5432` |
| **Redis Cluster** | `bitnamicharts/redis-cluster` | 6 Redis nodes (3 master + 3 replica) | **6** | `redis-cluster.database.svc.cluster.local:6379` |

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Namespace: database (22 Pods)"
        subgraph MongoDB Sharded - 11 Pods
            Mongos[Mongos x2] --> ConfigSrv[(Config Server x3)]
            Mongos --> Shard0[(Shard0: 3 Data Nodes)]
            Mongos --> Shard1[(Shard1: 3 Data Nodes)]
        end
        subgraph PostgreSQL HA - 5 Pods
            Pgpool[Pgpool x2] -->|Write| PgPrimary[(Primary)]
            Pgpool -->|Read| PgStandby1[(Standby 1)]
            Pgpool -->|Read| PgStandby2[(Standby 2)]
        end
        subgraph Redis Cluster - 6 Pods
            RM1[Master 1] <--> RS1[Replica 1]
            RM2[Master 2] <--> RS2[Replica 2]
            RM3[Master 3] <--> RS3[Replica 3]
        end
    end
```

### Environment Setup and Installation Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** Prepare required tooling and infra.
- **2. Clone demo source:**
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/system-design-mastery/3-complex-applications-and-helm-charts
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Deploy MongoDB Sharded:**
  ```bash
  cd mongodb-sharded
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  ```
- **4. Deploy PostgreSQL HA:**
  ```bash
  cd ../postgresql-ha
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  ```
- **5. Deploy Redis Cluster:**
  ```bash
  cd ../redis-cluster
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  ```
- **6. Success checks:**
  ```bash
  kubectl get pods -n database
  kubectl get pvc -n database
  kubectl get svc -n database
  ```

### Application Testing

- **Step 1 - MongoDB sharding check:**
  ```bash
  kubectl run mongo-client --rm -it --image=bitnamilegacy/mongodb-sharded:8.0.13-debian-12-r0 \
    -n database -- mongosh \
    mongodb://root:root123@mongodb-sharded-mongodb-sharded:27017/admin
  ```
  In `mongosh`:
  ```javascript
  sh.status()
  use demo
  sh.shardCollection("demo.orders", { _id: "hashed" })
  for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) db.orders.insertOne({ _id: i, name: "item" + i })
  db.orders.getShardDistribution()
  ```
- **Step 2 - PostgreSQL failover check:**
  ```bash
  kubectl run pg-client --rm -it --image=bitnamilegacy/postgresql-repmgr:17.6.0-debian-12-r2 \
    -n database --env="PGPASSWORD=postgres123" -- \
    psql -h postgresql-ha-pgpool -U postgres -d demo_db -c "SELECT inet_server_addr(), version();"
  kubectl delete pod -n database postgresql-ha-postgresql-0
  kubectl get pods -n database -l app.kubernetes.io/component=postgresql -w
  ```
- **Step 3 - Redis MOVED redirect check:**
  ```bash
  kubectl exec -it -n database redis-cluster-0 -- redis-cli -a redis123 -c SET "user:100" "alice"
  kubectl exec -it -n database redis-cluster-0 -- redis-cli -a redis123 -c GET "user:100"
  ```
- **Step 4 - PVC persistence check:**
  ```bash
  kubectl get pvc -n database
  kubectl delete pod -n database redis-cluster-0
  kubectl exec -it -n database redis-cluster-0 -- redis-cli -a redis123 GET "user:100"
  ```

## III. Core Concepts

- ***Helm***: Kubernetes package manager that renders chart templates with `values.yaml` into final manifests.
- ***Chart***: Reusable deployment package containing templates + defaults.
- ***Release***: An installed chart instance with revision history and rollback support.
- ***OCI Registry***: Helm chart distribution through OCI (`oci://`) registries.
- ***StatefulSet***: Stable identity + storage for stateful workloads.
- ***Headless Service***: `clusterIP: None`, resolves Pod-specific records instead of load balancing.
- ***volumeClaimTemplates***: Auto-generates one PVC per StatefulSet replica.

**When to use Helm:**
- Multi-resource stacks (DB HA, monitoring, ingress) that need consistent config.

**When Helm may be overkill:**
- Very small apps with only 1-2 simple manifests.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

Scope: Security, storage, and network boundaries.

- **Secrets outside Git:** use `existingSecret` and secret manager integration.
- **Real storage planning:** set PVC size, expansion strategy, backups, and realistic requests/limits.
- **Network segmentation:** apply `NetworkPolicy` to restrict DB ports to trusted namespaces only.

## V. Applications in Real Systems

Examples below are illustrative only, not verified internal architecture disclosures.

1. **Grab (illustrative)** - Helm-driven standardized stateful clusters across regions.
2. **Shopee (illustrative)** - fast DB failover for critical transactional flows.
3. **Pinterest (illustrative)** - Redis cluster + persistent stateful operations for scale-out caching.

translations.value: Ứng dụng phức tạp và Helm Chart

Triển khai ba cụm database chuẩn production trên Kubernetes chỉ bằng một lệnh Helm: MongoDB Sharded, PostgreSQL HA và Redis Cluster — sử dụng Bitnami Helm Charts qua OCI registry, cấu hình High Availability thật sự.

## I. Lời mở đầu

Chạy ***MySQL*** bằng một ***Pod*** trần và ***NestJS*** bằng một ***Deployment*** vài ***replica*** là đủ để demo, nhưng đi phỏng vấn ***Senior Backend*** sẽ bị hỏi ngay: *"production của em có 3 node ***MongoDB*** làm ***Replica Set*** + ***Sharding*** theo ***Shard Key***, ***Primary*** chết thì ***Failover*** trong bao lâu?"*, rồi *"thêm ***PostgreSQL*** với ***Primary–Standby***, ***Redis*** dạng ***Cluster*** 6 node chia ***Slot*** — một cụm bạn gõ tay bao nhiêu ***Manifest***?"*. Tự viết ***StatefulSet*** + ***Headless Service*** + ***Init Container*** + ***ConfigMap*** + ***Secret*** cho một cụm ***Database*** — một buổi chiều chưa xong, và 90% khả năng sai ***Hostname Resolution*** giữa các ***Replica*** hoặc quên field `volumeClaimTemplates` khiến dữ liệu bay theo ***Pod***.

Ngành đã giải quyết chỗ này bằng một ***Package Manager*** chuyên cho ***K8s***: ***Helm***. Giống như `brew` cho macOS hay `npm` cho Node.js, ***Helm*** đóng gói hàng chục ***Manifest*** thành một ***Chart*** có ***Values*** để override — chạy `helm install`, toàn bộ cụm tự dựng lên theo đúng kiến trúc đã được cộng đồng kiểm chứng. Trong hệ sinh thái này, ***Bitnami*** là đơn vị bán ***Chart Database*** được dùng nhiều nhất thế giới: ***MongoDB Sharded***, ***PostgreSQL HA***, ***Redis Cluster*** đều có ***Chart*** ***production-ready*** với ***StatefulSet***, ***PersistentVolumeClaim***, ***Health Check***, ***Metrics Exporter*** cài sẵn.

## II. Bản chất

Ba cụm cùng nằm trong ***Namespace*** `database` trên ***Cluster*** ***Minikube*** hoặc ***DOKS***. Mỗi cụm có ***Endpoint*** cố định qua ***Kubernetes DNS*** để ***Backend*** gọi vào:
- ***MongoDB Sharded*** (11 ***Pod***): 2 ***Shard*** × 3 ***Data Node*** + 3 ***Config Server*** + 2 ***Mongos Router***. ***Endpoint***: `mongodb-sharded-mongodb-sharded.database.svc.cluster.local:27017`.
- ***PostgreSQL HA*** (5 ***Pod***): 3 ***PostgreSQL-Repmgr*** (1 ***Primary*** + 2 ***Standby***) + 2 ***Pgpool***. ***Endpoint***: `postgresql-ha-pgpool.database.svc.cluster.local:5432`.
- ***Redis Cluster*** (6 ***Pod***): 6 ***Node Redis*** (3 ***Master*** + 3 ***Slave***, ***Shard*** tự động). ***Endpoint***: `redis-cluster.database.svc.cluster.local:6379`.

Clone tại [đây](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/system-design-mastery/complex-applications-and-helm-charts)

| Cụm | Chart OCI | Thành phần | Tổng Pod | Endpoint trong cluster |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **MongoDB Sharded** | `bitnamicharts/mongodb-sharded` | 2 Shard × 3 data node + 3 ConfigServer + 2 Mongos | **11** | `mongodb-sharded-mongodb-sharded.database.svc.cluster.local:27017` |
| **PostgreSQL HA** | `bitnamicharts/postgresql-ha` | 3 `postgresql-repmgr` (1 Primary + 2 Standby) + 2 Pgpool | **5** | `postgresql-ha-pgpool.database.svc.cluster.local:5432` |
| **Redis Cluster** | `bitnamicharts/redis-cluster` | 6 node Redis (3 Master + 3 Slave, shard tự động) | **6** | `redis-cluster.database.svc.cluster.local:6379` |

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Namespace: database (22 Pod)"
        subgraph MongoDB Sharded - 11 Pod
            Mongos[Mongos Router x2] --> ConfigSrv[(Config Server x3)]
            Mongos --> Shard0[(Shard0: 3 Data Node)]
            Mongos --> Shard1[(Shard1: 3 Data Node)]
        end

        subgraph PostgreSQL HA - 5 Pod
            Pgpool[Pgpool x2] -->|Write| PgPrimary[(Primary)]
            Pgpool -->|Read| PgStandby1[(Standby 1)]
            Pgpool -->|Read| PgStandby2[(Standby 2)]
        end

        subgraph Redis Cluster - 6 Pod
            RM1[Master 1] <--> RS1[Slave 1]
            RM2[Master 2] <--> RS2[Slave 2]
            RM3[Master 3] <--> RS3[Slave 3]
        end
    end
```

### Chuẩn bị Môi trường và Luồng Cài đặt

- **1. Prerequisites:** Chuẩn bị đầy đủ công cụ/hạ tầng theo yêu cầu của bài.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source để đọc đúng context code:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/system-design-mastery/3-complex-applications-and-helm-charts
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Clone repo và vào thư mục bài học:**
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/system-design-mastery/complex-applications-and-helm-charts
  ```
  Mỗi thư mục con (`mongodb-sharded`, `postgresql-ha`, `redis-cluster`) có đúng 4 file: **`values.origin.yaml`** (bản sao nguyên vẹn từ ***Bitnami GitHub*** để tham chiếu), **`values.yaml`** (***override*** — chỉ chứa những dòng cần đổi), **`run.sh`** / **`run.ps1`** (***script deploy***).
- **4. Deploy MongoDB Sharded:**

  ```bash
  cd mongodb-sharded
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  ```
  ***Script*** làm 3 việc: tạo ***Namespace*** `database`, chạy `helm upgrade --install mongodb-sharded oci://registry-1.docker.io/bitnamicharts/mongodb-sharded -n database --values values.yaml --wait`, rồi in trạng thái ***Pod*** + ***Endpoint*** + ***Password***.
- **5. Deploy PostgreSQL HA:**

  ```bash
  cd ../postgresql-ha
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  ```
  Theo `values.yaml`: `postgresql.replicaCount: 3` (1 ***Primary*** + 2 ***Standby*** qua ***Repmgr***), `pgpool.replicaCount: 2`, ***credentials*** `postgres/postgres123`, ***database*** `demo_db`.
- **6. Deploy Redis Cluster:**

  ```bash
  cd ../redis-cluster
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  ```
  Theo `values.yaml`: `cluster.nodes: 6`, `cluster.replicas: 1` (3 ***Master*** + 3 ***Slave***), `password: "redis123"`.
- **7. Tín hiệu thành công:**
  ```bash
  kubectl get pods -n database
  kubectl get pvc -n database
  kubectl get svc -n database
  ```
  `kubectl get pods -n database` trả về **22 Pod** (11 + 5 + 6) đều **Ready**. `kubectl get pvc -n database` cho thấy các ***PersistentVolumeClaim*** 8Gi đã được `Bound`. `kubectl get svc -n database` hiện các ***Headless Service*** + ***ClusterIP Service*** cho từng ***Release***.
### Kiểm thử ứng dụng

- **Bước 1:** Kết nối ***MongoDB Sharded*** qua ***Mongos***:
  ```bash
  kubectl run mongo-client --rm -it --image=bitnamilegacy/mongodb-sharded:8.0.13-debian-12-r0 \
    -n database -- mongosh \
    mongodb://root:root123@mongodb-sharded-mongodb-sharded:27017/admin
  ```
  Trong shell `mongosh`:
  ```javascript
  sh.status()
  use demo
  sh.shardCollection("demo.orders", { _id: "hashed" })
  for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) db.orders.insertOne({ _id: i, name: "item" + i })
  db.orders.getShardDistribution()
  ```

  *Kết luận:* `sh.status()` hiện 2 ***Shard*** `shard0`, `shard1`; sau khi insert 1000 ***document***, `getShardDistribution()` cho thấy dữ liệu được chia tương đối đều giữa hai ***Shard*** — minh chứng ***Hashed Sharding*** đã hoạt động.

- **Bước 2:** Kết nối ***PostgreSQL HA*** qua ***Pgpool*** và test ***Failover***:
  ```bash
  kubectl run pg-client --rm -it --image=bitnamilegacy/postgresql-repmgr:17.6.0-debian-12-r2 \
    -n database --env="PGPASSWORD=postgres123" -- \
    psql -h postgresql-ha-pgpool -U postgres -d demo_db -c "SELECT inet_server_addr(), version();"
  ```
  Xóa ***Primary*** để test ***Failover***:
  ```bash
  kubectl delete pod -n database postgresql-ha-postgresql-0
  kubectl get pods -n database -l app.kubernetes.io/component=postgresql -w
  ```
  Trong **10–20 giây**: ***Repmgr*** phát hiện mất ***Primary*** → ***promote*** `postgresql-ha-postgresql-1` lên ***Primary*** → ***Pgpool*** reload danh sách ***Node***.

  *Kết luận:* Chạy lại lệnh `psql`, `inet_server_addr()` giờ trả ***IP*** của ***Node*** mới — ứng dụng **không đổi ***Connection String*****, chỉ đổi ***Primary*** bên dưới. Đây là giá trị cốt lõi của ***PostgreSQL HA*** với ***Repmgr*** + ***Pgpool***.

- **Bước 3:** Kết nối ***Redis Cluster*** và thấy ***MOVED Redirect***:
  ```bash
  kubectl exec -it -n database redis-cluster-0 -- redis-cli -a redis123 -c \
    SET "user:100" "alice"
  kubectl exec -it -n database redis-cluster-0 -- redis-cli -a redis123 -c \
    GET "user:100"
  ```
  Flag `-c` bật ***Cluster Mode*** trong `redis-cli`. Key `user:100` hash ra ***Slot*** `9842`, thuộc dải ***Master*** 2.

  *Kết luận:* Nếu gõ vào ***Master*** sai, server trả ***`-MOVED 9842 <ip>:6379`*** → `redis-cli -c` tự follow ***Redirect*** và lấy dữ liệu. Không có `-c`, ***client*** sẽ lỗi `MOVED`.

- **Bước 4:** Xem ***Persistent Volume Claim*** (***PVC***) và test dữ liệu sống sót:
  ```bash
  kubectl get pvc -n database
  kubectl delete pod -n database redis-cluster-0
  kubectl exec -it -n database redis-cluster-0 -- redis-cli -a redis123 GET "user:100"
  ```

  *Kết luận:* ***Pod*** `redis-cluster-0` bị xóa, ***StatefulSet*** re-create một ***Pod*** cùng tên, gắn lại đúng ***PVC*** cũ → dữ liệu `user:100` vẫn còn. Đây là điều ***Pod*** trần ở bài 1 không làm được.

Sau các luồng trên, **III** tóm tắt **Helm / Chart / StatefulSet**; **IV** là rủi ro **production** (bí mật, đĩa, policy, override tối thiểu).

## III. Các khái niệm cốt lõi

- ***Helm***: ***Package Manager*** cho ***Kubernetes***. Đọc ***Chart*** (thư mục chứa ***template Go***), trộn với ***`values.yaml`***, render ra ***Manifest*** cuối cùng và gửi lên ***`kube-apiserver`***. Không có ***daemon*** nào chạy trong ***Cluster*** kể từ ***Helm 3*** — toàn bộ ***state*** lưu trong ***Secret*** dưới dạng ***Release History***.
- ***Chart***: Một ***package*** chứa các file ***template YAML*** + `values.yaml` mặc định. Cùng một ***Chart*** chạy được trên ***Minikube***, ***EKS***, ***DOKS*** — chỉ khác `values.yaml`.
- ***Release***: Mỗi `helm install` tạo một ***Release***. `helm list -n database` hiện ***Revision*** hiện tại; `helm rollback <release> <revision>` quay về bản cũ trong vài giây.
- ***OCI Registry*** (***Helm 3.8+***): ***Chart*** nằm ngay trong ***OCI Registry*** (***Docker Hub***, ***GHCR***, ***ECR***). `oci://registry-1.docker.io/bitnamicharts/mongodb-sharded` đi qua đúng ***pipeline image*** — tận dụng ***cache***, ***signing***, ***authentication*** chung.
- ***Bitnami***: Đơn vị duy trì bộ ***Chart Database*** được coi là tham chiếu công nghiệp: ***test matrix*** rộng, ***security hardening***, hỗ trợ ***Prometheus Metrics*** sẵn.
- ***StatefulSet***: Khác ***Deployment*** ở chỗ mỗi ***Replica*** có ***identity*** ổn định (tên cố định `pod-0`, `pod-1`...) và ***disk*** bền vững qua ***PVC***. Bắt buộc cho ***Stateful Workload*** (***MongoDB***, ***PostgreSQL***, ***Redis***).
- ***Headless Service***: ***Service*** với `clusterIP: None`. ***DNS*** không cân bằng tải mà trả về ***IP*** của từng ***Pod***: `mongodb-sharded-shard0-data-0.mongodb-sharded-headless.database.svc.cluster.local`. Cơ sở để ***Repmgr*** / ***MongoDB Replica*** nói chuyện với nhau bằng ***hostname*** ổn định.
- ***PersistentVolumeClaim template***: ***StatefulSet*** có field `volumeClaimTemplates` — mỗi ***Replica*** tự sinh một ***PVC*** tên `<pvc-name>-<statefulset>-<index>`. ***Pod*** luôn ***mount*** đúng ***PVC*** cũ kể cả khi ***reschedule*** sang ***Node*** khác.

**Khi nào dùng ***Helm***:**
- ***Chart*** có **≥ 10 ***Manifest*** liên quan** cần config đồng bộ (***Database HA***, ***Monitoring Stack***, ***Ingress Controller***).

**Khi nào KHÔNG dùng ***Helm***:**
- Ứng dụng chỉ có 1–2 ***Manifest*** (1 ***Pod*** + 1 ***Service***) — ***overhead template*** lớn hơn lợi ích.

## IV. Kỹ thuật nâng cao

Phạm vi: Bảo mật chart, đĩa & ranh giới mạng

- **Bí mật không nằm trong Git — `existingSecret` + secret manager.**
  - Mật khẩu demo trong `values.yaml` chỉ cho lab; production cần tham chiếu **Secret** (hoặc **External Secrets** + Vault/Cloud SM). Đồng thời giữ **override tối thiểu**: fork cả `values.origin.yaml` dễ lệch key khi chart nâng cấp.
  - **Trade-off:** pipeline phức tạp hơn, nhưng tránh lộ credential và tránh `helm upgrade` vỡ vì thiếu field mới.
- **PVC, mở rộng đĩa và requests/limits thật sự.**
  - `persistence.size` cố định; vượt ngưỡng cần **StorageClass** `allowVolumeExpansion`, chỉnh PVC và kế hoạch restart. Song song, preset resource “nano/none” của chart không đủ cho shard/primary thật — phải đặt CPU/RAM tối thiểu và limits để một query nặng không **OOM** cả node.
  - **Trade-off:** cost tài nguyên tăng; đổi lại cụm DB không chết vì “đĩa đầy im lặng” hoặc neighbor noise.
- **NetworkPolicy khóa namespace `database`.**
  - Mặc định mọi pod trong cluster có thể quét cổng DB. Production nên **NetworkPolicy** chỉ cho phép namespace ứng dụng vào `3306/5432/6379/27017`.
  - **Trade-off:** debug khó hơn (phải nới rule có kiểm soát), nhưng giảm bề mặt tấn công ngang cluster.

## V. Ứng dụng trong hệ thống thực tế

Các **case** dưới đây mang tên nền tảng quen thuộc chỉ để **minh hoạ — giả định** cách áp dụng lý thuyết bài học; **không** mô tả kiến trúc nội bộ đã được công bố và **không** phải phát ngôn đại diện doanh nghiệp.

1. **Grab (minh hoạ — giả định)**
   - **Tình huống:** Nhiều region, mỗi nơi cần cụm stateful tương đồng để đồng bộ vận hành.
   - **Bài toán hệ thống:** Viết tay hàng chục manifest cho mỗi region không bền vững.
   - **Vận dụng lý thuyết:** **Helm** + chart tham chiếu (Bitnami/…) + `values` theo region — đúng tinh thần “một chart, nhiều bản triển khai”.

2. **Shopee (minh hoạ — giả định)**
   - **Tình huống:** Luồng thanh toán cần giảm thời gian mất **primary** DB.
   - **Bài toán hệ thống:** Failover tay quá lâu so với SLO nghiệp vụ.
   - **Vận dụng lý thuyết:** Mô hình **PostgreSQL HA** (repmgr/pgpool trong demo) minh hoạ “promote nhanh + connection string qua pool” — không khẳng định cấu hình production thực tế.

3. **Pinterest (minh hoạ — giả định)**
   - **Tình huống:** Dữ liệu session/cache lớn, cần phân mảnh và khả năng sống sót khi node chết.
   - **Bài toán hệ thống:** Một nút Redis đơn không đủ RAM và SPOF.
   - **Vận dụng lý thuyết:** **Redis Cluster** + **PVC** + **StatefulSet** trong bài minh hoạ hướng scale-out có đĩa bền — ví dụ định hướng, không mô tả stack nội bộ Pinterest.
Complex Applications and Helm Charts
Deploy three production-style database clusters on Kubernetes with Helm: MongoDB Sharded, PostgreSQL HA, and Redis Cluster - using Bitnami OCI charts and practical high-availability configuration.

## I. Introduction

Running a single MySQL Pod and a small NestJS Deployment is enough for demos, but senior-level interviews quickly move to real operations:
- How do you run MongoDB with replica sets and sharding?
- How fast is PostgreSQL failover from primary to standby?
- How do you deploy Redis Cluster with slot distribution and replication?

Hand-writing all Kubernetes manifests for stateful database clusters is slow and error-prone. Common mistakes include unstable hostnames between replicas or missing `volumeClaimTemplates`, which can lead to data loss.

This is exactly why teams use ***Helm***. Like `npm` for Node.js, Helm packages many Kubernetes manifests into reusable ***Charts*** with configurable ***Values***. With one `helm install`, you can deploy proven architecture patterns maintained by the community.

## II. Essence

We deploy three clusters inside namespace `database` (Minikube or DOKS):
- ***MongoDB Sharded*** (11 Pods): 2 shards x 3 data nodes + 3 config servers + 2 mongos routers  
  Endpoint: `mongodb-sharded-mongodb-sharded.database.svc.cluster.local:27017`
- ***PostgreSQL HA*** (5 Pods): 3 repmgr PostgreSQL nodes (1 primary + 2 standby) + 2 pgpool  
  Endpoint: `postgresql-ha-pgpool.database.svc.cluster.local:5432`
- ***Redis Cluster*** (6 Pods): 3 master + 3 replica nodes  
  Endpoint: `redis-cluster.database.svc.cluster.local:6379`

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/system-design-mastery/complex-applications-and-helm-charts)

| Cluster | OCI Chart | Components | Total Pods | In-cluster Endpoint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **MongoDB Sharded** | `bitnamicharts/mongodb-sharded` | 2 shards x 3 data nodes + 3 config servers + 2 mongos | **11** | `mongodb-sharded-mongodb-sharded.database.svc.cluster.local:27017` |
| **PostgreSQL HA** | `bitnamicharts/postgresql-ha` | 3 `postgresql-repmgr` + 2 pgpool | **5** | `postgresql-ha-pgpool.database.svc.cluster.local:5432` |
| **Redis Cluster** | `bitnamicharts/redis-cluster` | 6 Redis nodes (3 master + 3 replica) | **6** | `redis-cluster.database.svc.cluster.local:6379` |

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Namespace: database (22 Pods)"
        subgraph MongoDB Sharded - 11 Pods
            Mongos[Mongos x2] --> ConfigSrv[(Config Server x3)]
            Mongos --> Shard0[(Shard0: 3 Data Nodes)]
            Mongos --> Shard1[(Shard1: 3 Data Nodes)]
        end
        subgraph PostgreSQL HA - 5 Pods
            Pgpool[Pgpool x2] -->|Write| PgPrimary[(Primary)]
            Pgpool -->|Read| PgStandby1[(Standby 1)]
            Pgpool -->|Read| PgStandby2[(Standby 2)]
        end
        subgraph Redis Cluster - 6 Pods
            RM1[Master 1] <--> RS1[Replica 1]
            RM2[Master 2] <--> RS2[Replica 2]
            RM3[Master 3] <--> RS3[Replica 3]
        end
    end
```

### Environment Setup and Installation Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** Prepare required tooling and infra.
- **2. Clone demo source:**
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/system-design-mastery/3-complex-applications-and-helm-charts
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Deploy MongoDB Sharded:**
  ```bash
  cd mongodb-sharded
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  ```
- **4. Deploy PostgreSQL HA:**
  ```bash
  cd ../postgresql-ha
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  ```
- **5. Deploy Redis Cluster:**
  ```bash
  cd ../redis-cluster
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  ```
- **6. Success checks:**
  ```bash
  kubectl get pods -n database
  kubectl get pvc -n database
  kubectl get svc -n database
  ```

### Application Testing

- **Step 1 - MongoDB sharding check:**
  ```bash
  kubectl run mongo-client --rm -it --image=bitnamilegacy/mongodb-sharded:8.0.13-debian-12-r0 \
    -n database -- mongosh \
    mongodb://root:root123@mongodb-sharded-mongodb-sharded:27017/admin
  ```
  In `mongosh`:
  ```javascript
  sh.status()
  use demo
  sh.shardCollection("demo.orders", { _id: "hashed" })
  for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) db.orders.insertOne({ _id: i, name: "item" + i })
  db.orders.getShardDistribution()
  ```
- **Step 2 - PostgreSQL failover check:**
  ```bash
  kubectl run pg-client --rm -it --image=bitnamilegacy/postgresql-repmgr:17.6.0-debian-12-r2 \
    -n database --env="PGPASSWORD=postgres123" -- \
    psql -h postgresql-ha-pgpool -U postgres -d demo_db -c "SELECT inet_server_addr(), version();"
  kubectl delete pod -n database postgresql-ha-postgresql-0
  kubectl get pods -n database -l app.kubernetes.io/component=postgresql -w
  ```
- **Step 3 - Redis MOVED redirect check:**
  ```bash
  kubectl exec -it -n database redis-cluster-0 -- redis-cli -a redis123 -c SET "user:100" "alice"
  kubectl exec -it -n database redis-cluster-0 -- redis-cli -a redis123 -c GET "user:100"
  ```
- **Step 4 - PVC persistence check:**
  ```bash
  kubectl get pvc -n database
  kubectl delete pod -n database redis-cluster-0
  kubectl exec -it -n database redis-cluster-0 -- redis-cli -a redis123 GET "user:100"
  ```

## III. Core Concepts

- ***Helm***: Kubernetes package manager that renders chart templates with `values.yaml` into final manifests.
- ***Chart***: Reusable deployment package containing templates + defaults.
- ***Release***: An installed chart instance with revision history and rollback support.
- ***OCI Registry***: Helm chart distribution through OCI (`oci://`) registries.
- ***StatefulSet***: Stable identity + storage for stateful workloads.
- ***Headless Service***: `clusterIP: None`, resolves Pod-specific records instead of load balancing.
- ***volumeClaimTemplates***: Auto-generates one PVC per StatefulSet replica.

**When to use Helm:**
- Multi-resource stacks (DB HA, monitoring, ingress) that need consistent config.

**When Helm may be overkill:**
- Very small apps with only 1-2 simple manifests.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

Scope: Security, storage, and network boundaries.

- **Secrets outside Git:** use `existingSecret` and secret manager integration.
- **Real storage planning:** set PVC size, expansion strategy, backups, and realistic requests/limits.
- **Network segmentation:** apply `NetworkPolicy` to restrict DB ports to trusted namespaces only.

## V. Applications in Real Systems

Examples below are illustrative only, not verified internal architecture disclosures.

1. **Grab (illustrative)** - Helm-driven standardized stateful clusters across regions.
2. **Shopee (illustrative)** - fast DB failover for critical transactional flows.
3. **Pinterest (illustrative)** - Redis cluster + persistent stateful operations for scale-out caching.

contents.title: Kubernetes on Cloud: Practical Deployment with DigitalOcean
contents.description: Deploy a NestJS backend + MySQL + Redis on DigitalOcean Kubernetes (DOKS) with NGINX Ingress Controller, Cert-Manager, and Let's Encrypt for real-domain HTTPS automation.
contents.body:
## I. Introduction

Minikube is excellent for learning, but production questions are different:
- How does a request reach your app from the public internet?
- Where is TLS terminated?
- Who handles failover when Pods die?

Building Kubernetes manually on raw VMs is heavy operational work (`kubeadm`, etcd, control-plane HA, cert rotation). Managed Kubernetes (DOKS/EKS/GKE/AKS) offloads control-plane management so teams can focus on workloads and platform controllers.

## II. Essence

Target flow: ***Internet*** -> ***DigitalOcean Load Balancer*** -> ***NGINX Ingress Controller*** -> `backend-service` -> 3 backend Pods -> `mysql-service` / `redis-service`.  
***Cert-Manager*** integrates with ***Let's Encrypt*** to issue and renew TLS certificates.

- ***NGINX Ingress Controller*** (2 replicas): routes HTTPS traffic into the cluster.
- ***Cert-Manager***: automatic certificate issuance and renewal through ACME.
- ***Backend*** (NestJS, 3 replicas): API service with MySQL + Redis.
- ***Client*** access: `https://api.your-domain.com`.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/system-design-mastery/kubernetes-on-cloud)

| Component | Technology | Role | Port / Namespace |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cluster** | DOKS | Managed Kubernetes with dedicated node pools | - |
| **CLI** | `doctl`, `kubectl`, `helm` | Cluster access and deployment tooling | - |
| **Ingress Controller** | NGINX Ingress | HTTPS routing and LB integration | 80 / 443 (`ingress-nginx`) |
| **Cert Manager** | cert-manager | ACME automation for TLS | `cert-manager` |
| **Backend** | NestJS | API server, 3 replicas | 3000 |
| **Database** | MySQL 8.0 | Persistent app data | 3306 |
| **Cache** | Redis 7 | Short-lived cache | 6379 |

```mermaid
graph LR
    Internet((Internet)) --> LB[DO Load Balancer :443]
    LB --> Ingress[NGINX Ingress Controller x2]
    Ingress -->|TLS Termination| SVC[backend-service :3000]
    SVC --> Pod1(Backend Pod 1)
    SVC --> Pod2(Backend Pod 2)
    SVC --> Pod3(Backend Pod 3)
    Pod1 --> MySQL[(mysql-service :3306)]
    Pod1 --> Redis[(redis-service :6379)]
    CertMgr[Cert-Manager] -.->|ACME HTTP-01| Ingress
    CertMgr -.->|Let's Encrypt| LE((Let's Encrypt))
```

### Environment Setup and Installation Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** Prepare all required cloud accounts and tools.
- **2. Clone demo source:**
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/system-design-mastery/4-kubernetes-on-cloud
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Create DOKS cluster:** choose stable Kubernetes version and create node pools (edge/system separation).
- **4. Configure `kubectl`:**
  ```bash
  doctl kubernetes cluster kubeconfig save <cluster-name>
  kubectl get nodes
  ```
- **5. Install cert-manager:**
  ```bash
  cd cert-manager
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  kubectl get pods -n cert-manager
  ```
- **6. Install NGINX ingress controller:**
  ```bash
  cd ../nginx-ingress-controller
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  kubectl get svc -n ingress-nginx -w
  ```
- **7. Point DNS A record to ingress external IP.**
- **8. Apply issuer + data tier + backend + ingress:**
  ```bash
  kubectl apply -f cluster-issuer.yaml
  kubectl apply -f mysql-pod.yaml
  kubectl apply -f mysql-service.yaml
  kubectl apply -f redis-pod.yaml
  kubectl apply -f redis-service.yaml
  kubectl apply -f backend-deployment.yaml
  kubectl apply -f backend-service.yaml
  kubectl apply -f ingress.yaml
  ```
- **9. Verify status:**
  ```bash
  kubectl get pods
  kubectl get ingress
  kubectl get certificate
  ```

### Application Testing

- **Step 1 - Certificate readiness:**
  ```bash
  kubectl get certificate
  kubectl describe certificate backend-tls-secret
  ```
- **Step 2 - HTTPS health check:**
  ```bash
  curl -s https://api.your-domain.com/health
  ```
- **Step 3 - Create data over HTTPS:**
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST https://api.your-domain.com/items \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"digitalocean"}'
  ```
- **Step 4 - Verify cache flow:**
  ```bash
  curl -s https://api.your-domain.com/items
  curl -s https://api.your-domain.com/items
  ```

## III. Core Concepts

- ***Managed Kubernetes***: cloud provider manages control plane, team manages workloads.
- ***Ingress***: host/path routing layer in front of services.
- ***Ingress Controller***: runtime implementation of ingress rules (NGINX).
- ***Cert-Manager***: certificate lifecycle automation via ACME.
- ***ClusterIssuer vs Issuer***: cluster-wide vs namespace-scoped certificate issuers.
- ***HTTP-01 / DNS-01*** challenges: domain ownership verification methods.
- ***Node Pool***: isolated worker groups for workload separation.
- ***TLS Termination***: HTTPS decrypted at ingress, internal traffic continues to backend.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

Scope: Production edge hardening and stateful reliability.

- Use **StatefulSet/PVC** or managed DB services for MySQL/Redis in production.
- Use proper **Secrets** and external secret managers instead of plaintext credentials.
- Define **readiness/liveness probes** and resources to avoid rollout 502s and noisy-neighbor failures.
- Respect Let's Encrypt **rate limits** and use staging issuers during validation.

## V. Applications in Real Systems

Illustrative examples only (not official architecture disclosures):

1. **Shopee (illustrative)** - centralized ingress + automated TLS across many hosts.
2. **Grab (illustrative)** - separate edge and compute node pools for performance isolation.
3. **GitLab (illustrative)** - automated certificate issuance for many domains.

translations.value: Kubernetes trên Cloud: Triển khai thực tế với DigitalOcean

Triển khai NestJS backend + MySQL + Redis lên DigitalOcean Kubernetes (DOKS) với NGINX Ingress Controller, Cert-Manager và Let's Encrypt — domain thật, HTTPS tự động, Load Balancer gắn sticky sessions.

## I. Lời mở đầu

Chạy ***Kubernetes*** trên máy cá nhân bằng ***Minikube*** là sân tập tốt, nhưng đi phỏng vấn ***Senior Backend*** không ai hỏi *"em chạy `kubectl port-forward` ra localhost thế nào"*. Câu hỏi thật là: *"Anh ***deploy backend*** này lên ***production***, user ở Singapore gõ `api.domain.com` thì ***request*** đi qua những đâu, ***HTTPS*** cấp thế nào, ***Pod*** chết thì ai hứng?"*. Người chưa tự tay dựng qua một lần sẽ trả lời lủng củng: nhầm giữa ***Ingress*** và ***Service***, không biết ***Load Balancer*** ở đâu ra, tưởng ***SSL*** phải mua từ ***provider*** và update tay mỗi năm.

Tự dựng ***Kubernetes Cluster*** trên ***Bare-metal*** hay ***VM*** thuần thì nặng: phải cài `kubeadm`, quản ***etcd***, chứng chỉ ***TLS*** nội bộ, vá ***kernel***, lo ***High Availability*** cho ***Control Plane*** — mất hàng tuần trước khi chạm đến một dòng nghiệp vụ. ***Managed Kubernetes*** (***DOKS***, ***EKS***, ***GKE***, ***AKS***) dựng sẵn ***Control Plane*** và dán vào sẵn các mảnh hạ tầng: ***Load Balancer***, ***Block Storage***, ***VPC***, ***Firewall***. Bạn chỉ trả tiền cho ***Worker Nodes*** và tập trung đúng việc cần làm — ***deploy workload*** + cấu hình các ***Controller*** cần thiết.

## II. Bản chất

Kiến trúc đích: ***Internet*** → ***DigitalOcean Load Balancer*** → ***NGINX Ingress Controller*** → ***backend-service*** (***NodePort***) → 3 ***Backend Pod*** → ***mysql-service*** / ***redis-service*** (***ClusterIP***). ***Cert-Manager*** đứng bên cạnh, bắt tay với ***Let's Encrypt*** để sinh và gia hạn ***TLS Cert*** cho ***domain***:
- ***NGINX Ingress Controller*** (2 ***Replicas***): Điều phối ***traffic HTTPS*** vào ***Cluster***, tự tạo ***DO Load Balancer***.
- ***Cert-Manager***: Tự cấp + ***renew TLS Cert*** qua ***Let's Encrypt*** ***ACME Protocol***.
- ***Backend*** (***NestJS***, 3 ***Replicas***): ***API Server*** + ***MySQL*** + ***Redis*** — tái sử dụng ***Manifest*** từ bài 2.
- ***Client*** truy cập qua `https://api.your-domain.com` — ***HTTPS*** tự động, ***HTTP*** redirect sang ***HTTPS***.

Clone tại [đây](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/system-design-mastery/kubernetes-on-cloud)

| Thành phần | Công nghệ | Vai trò | Cổng / Namespace |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cluster** | ***DOKS*** (DigitalOcean Kubernetes) | ***Managed K8s***, 2 ***Node Pool***: `ingress-pool` + `system-pool` | — |
| **CLI** | `doctl` + `kubectl` + `helm` | Kết nối ***Cluster***, apply ***Manifest***, cài ***Helm Chart*** | — |
| **Ingress Controller** | ***NGINX Ingress Controller*** (Bitnami chart) | Điều phối ***traffic HTTPS***, tự tạo ***DO Load Balancer*** | **80** / **443** (ns `ingress-nginx`) |
| **Cert Manager** | ***Cert-Manager*** (Bitnami chart) | Tự cấp + ***renew TLS Cert*** qua ***Let's Encrypt*** | ns `cert-manager` |
| **Backend** | ***NestJS*** (`starci183/example-backend:latest`) | ***API Server***, 3 ***Replicas*** | **3000** (***NodePort*** 30000) |
| **Database** | ***MySQL 8.0*** | Lưu trữ dữ liệu, standalone ***Pod*** | **3306** (***ClusterIP***) |
| **Cache** | ***Redis 7*** | ***Cache*** danh sách item, ***TTL*** 60s | **6379** (***ClusterIP***) |

```mermaid
graph LR

    LB --> Ingress[NGINX Ingress Controller x2]
    Ingress -->|TLS Termination| SVC[backend-service :3000]
    SVC --> Pod1(Backend Pod 1)
    SVC --> Pod2(Backend Pod 2)
    SVC --> Pod3(Backend Pod 3)

    Pod1 --> Redis[(redis-service :6379)]

    CertMgr -.->|Let's Encrypt| LE((Let's Encrypt))
```

### Chuẩn bị Môi trường và Luồng Cài đặt

- **1. Prerequisites:** Chuẩn bị đầy đủ công cụ/hạ tầng theo yêu cầu của bài.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source để đọc đúng context code:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/system-design-mastery/4-kubernetes-on-cloud
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Tạo ***DOKS Cluster***:** Trên UI ***DigitalOcean***, chọn ***region*** gần người dùng, phiên bản ***K8s*** stable. Cấu hình **hai ***Node Pool***:**

  | Node Pool | Mục đích | Label |
  |---|---|---|
  | `ingress-pool` | Chạy ***NGINX Ingress Controller*** + ***Default Backend*** | `doks.digitalocean.com/node-pool: ingress-pool` |
  | `system-pool` | Chạy ***Cert-Manager*** và các ***workload*** hệ thống | `doks.digitalocean.com/node-pool: system-pool` |
- **4. Kết nối `kubectl` với ***Cluster***:**
  ```bash
  doctl kubernetes cluster kubeconfig save <cluster-name>
  kubectl get nodes
  ```
  Kết quả mong đợi: danh sách ***Worker Node*** trên ***DigitalOcean*** ở trạng thái **Ready**.
- **5. Cài ***Cert-Manager***:** Vào thư mục `cert-manager` và chạy ***script***:
  ```bash
  cd cert-manager
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  ```
  ```bash
  kubectl get pods -n cert-manager
  ```
  Kết quả mong đợi: 3 ***Pod*** (`cert-manager-*`, `cert-manager-webhook-*`, `cert-manager-cainjector-*`) đều **1/1 Running**.
- **6. Cài ***NGINX Ingress Controller***:**
  ```bash
  cd ../nginx-ingress-controller
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  ```
  Chờ ***DigitalOcean*** cấp ***External IP*** cho ***LoadBalancer Service***:
  ```bash
  kubectl get svc -n ingress-nginx -w
  ```
  Kết quả mong đợi: sau 1–2 phút, cột `EXTERNAL-IP` hiện một ***IP*** công khai. Ghi lại ***IP*** này.
- **7. Trỏ ***DNS A Record***:**

  | Type | Name | Value | TTL |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | A | `api` | `<EXTERNAL_IP>` | 300 |

  Kiểm tra ***propagation***:
  ```bash
  nslookup api.your-domain.com
  ```
- **8. Apply ***ClusterIssuer*** + tầng dữ liệu + ***Backend*** + ***Ingress***:**
  ```bash
  kubectl apply -f cluster-issuer.yaml
  kubectl apply -f mysql-pod.yaml
  kubectl apply -f mysql-service.yaml
  kubectl apply -f redis-pod.yaml
  kubectl apply -f redis-service.yaml
  kubectl apply -f backend-deployment.yaml
  kubectl apply -f backend-service.yaml
  kubectl apply -f ingress.yaml
  ```
- **9. Tín hiệu thành công:**
  ```bash
  kubectl get pods
  kubectl get ingress
  kubectl get certificate
  ```
  `kubectl get pods` cho thấy `mysql-pod`, `redis-pod` **Running**; ***Deployment*** `example-backend` **3/3 READY**. `kubectl get ingress` trả về `backend-ingress` với host `api.your-domain.com`. `kubectl get certificate` cho thấy `backend-tls-secret` **READY=True**.
### Kiểm thử ứng dụng

- **Bước 1:** Xác nhận ***Certificate*** đã cấp xong (***Cert-Manager*** mất khoảng 30s–2 phút):
  ```bash
  kubectl get certificate
  kubectl describe certificate backend-tls-secret
  ```

  *Kết luận:* `backend-tls-secret` **READY=True**. Nếu **READY=False** quá lâu, xem `kubectl get challenge` — 90% do ***DNS*** chưa trỏ đúng hoặc ***domain*** bị ***firewall*** chặn cổng **80**.

- **Bước 2:** ***Health Check*** qua ***HTTPS***. Dùng **Postman** gửi `GET` vào `https://api.your-domain.com/health`. Hoặc dùng `curl`:
  ```bash
  curl -s https://api.your-domain.com/health
  ```
  Kết quả mong đợi:
  ```json
  {
    "mysql": { "status": "connected", "itemCount": 0 },
    "redis": { "status": "connected" }
  }
  ```

  *Kết luận:* Trình duyệt hiện khóa xanh (***Certificate*** ký bởi ***Let's Encrypt***). ***Request HTTP*** tự ***redirect*** sang ***HTTPS*** nhờ ***annotation*** `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "true"`.

- **Bước 3:** Tạo dữ liệu qua ***HTTPS***. Dùng **Postman** gửi `POST` vào `https://api.your-domain.com/items` với header `Content-Type: application/json` và body `{ "name": "digitalocean" }`. Hoặc dùng `curl`:
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST https://api.your-domain.com/items \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"digitalocean"}'
  ```

  *Kết luận:* ***Backend*** trả về item vừa tạo kèm `id`, ***cache key*** `items:all` trong ***Redis*** bị ***invalidate***.

- **Bước 4:** Đọc dữ liệu (***Cache flow***):
  ```bash
  curl -s https://api.your-domain.com/items
  curl -s https://api.your-domain.com/items
  ```

  *Kết luận:* Lần 1 là ***Cache miss*** → ***Backend*** query ***MySQL***, cache kết quả vào ***Redis*** ***TTL*** 60s. Lần 2 (trong 60s) là ***Cache hit*** → ***Backend*** trả từ ***Redis***. Luồng đầy đủ: ***Client*** → ***DO Load Balancer*** → ***NGINX Ingress Controller*** (:443, ***TLS Termination***) → ***backend-service*** → ***Backend Pod*** → ***mysql-service*** / ***redis-service*** qua ***DNS*** nội bộ.

Sau luồng **HTTPS** thực tế, **III** giải thích **Ingress / Cert-Manager / Managed K8s**; **IV** nối các điểm production (state cho DB, secret, probe, giới hạn ACME).

## III. Các khái niệm cốt lõi

- ***Managed Kubernetes***: Nhà cung cấp quản ***Control Plane*** (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-scheduler`, `kube-controller-manager`). Bạn chỉ trả tiền ***Worker Nodes*** + ***LB*** / ***Storage***. Ví dụ: ***DOKS*** (DigitalOcean), ***EKS*** (AWS), ***GKE*** (Google), ***AKS*** (Azure).
- ***Ingress***: Một lớp trừu tượng giữa ***Cloud Load Balancer*** và ***Service*** nội bộ. Cho phép định tuyến theo ***host*** / ***path*** — một ***LB*** duy nhất phục vụ nhiều ***domain*** khác nhau. Không có ***Ingress***, mỗi ***Service LoadBalancer*** sinh một ***LB*** riêng → lãng phí tiền.
- ***Ingress Controller***: ***Pod*** thực thi logic ***Ingress*** — ***NGINX Ingress Controller*** là phổ biến nhất. Tự tạo ***Cloud Load Balancer*** khi ***Service*** kiểu ***LoadBalancer*** được apply.
- ***Cert-Manager***: ***Controller*** theo dõi ***CRD*** `Certificate` / `CertificateRequest` / `Order` / `Challenge` và điều khiển ***ACME Protocol*** nói chuyện với ***Let's Encrypt***. Tự ***renew*** khi ***cert*** còn 30 ngày trước hạn.
- ***ClusterIssuer*** vs ***Issuer***: ***ClusterIssuer*** có phạm vi ***Cluster*** (mọi ***Namespace*** đều dùng được). ***Issuer*** giới hạn một ***Namespace***.
- ***HTTP-01 Challenge***: ***Cert-Manager*** tạo tạm một ***Ingress Rule*** cho path `/.well-known/acme-challenge/<token>`, ***Let's Encrypt*** gõ vào ***domain*** qua cổng **80** để xác minh quyền sở hữu.
- ***DNS-01 Challenge***: Cần cho ***Wildcard Certificate*** (`*.your-domain.com`). ***Let's Encrypt*** bắt buộc xác minh qua ***DNS TXT Record***.
- ***Node Pool***: Nhóm ***Worker Node*** có cùng cấu hình. Tách `ingress-pool` và `system-pool` để ***traffic edge*** không tranh ***CPU*** với ***Backend*** nghiệp vụ.
- ***TLS Termination***: ***Ingress*** giải mã ***HTTPS*** rồi forward ***HTTP*** nội bộ xuống ***Backend*** — ***Backend*** không cần biết ***HTTPS***.

**Khi nào dùng ***Managed K8s***:**
- ***Production*** cần ***High Availability Control Plane***, tích hợp ***IAM*** / ***Load Balancer*** / ***Block Storage*** sẵn.

**Khi nào dùng ***Self-hosted K8s***:**
- Tổ chức có đội ***SRE*** chuyên trách, yêu cầu kiểm soát hoàn toàn ***Control Plane***, hoặc chạy trên ***Bare-metal*** / ***edge***.

## IV. Kỹ thuật nâng cao

Phạm vi: Biên HTTPS, state DB & giới hạn ACME

- **StatefulSet / DB managed + Secret thật — tránh “Ingress xịn nhưng DB pod trần”.**
  - Demo giữ MySQL/Redis dạng pod đơn; production nên **PVC + StatefulSet** hoặc **managed database** để backup/patch không nằm trên cùng lifecycle với app. Đồng thời bỏ mật khẩu plain-text trong manifest, dùng **Secret** + external manager.
  - **Trade-off:** chi phí dịch vụ và pipeline phức tạp hơn; đổi lại không mất dữ liệu khi reschedule và không lộ credential trong Git.
- **Probe gắn Ingress và tài nguyên pod — tránh 502 lúc rollout.**
  - Không **readiness** → NGINX vẫn forward vào replica chưa kết nối DB; không **limits** → leak RAM làm hàng xóm chết.
  - **Trade-off:** phải tune path `/health` và threshold; đây là bước bắt buộc khi TLS terminate tại edge nhưng nghiệp vụ phụ thuộc DB.
- **Giới hạn Let's Encrypt và chiến lược staging / DNS-01.**
  - Issuer production có **rate limit** theo domain; thử sai nhiều lần có thể khóa cấp chứng chỉ. Dùng **staging** khi thử pipeline; **DNS-01** khi cần wildcard.
  - **Trade-off:** staging không được browser trust; DNS-01 cần quyền ghi DNS tự động.

## V. Ứng dụng trong hệ thống thực tế

Các **case** dưới đây mang tên nền tảng quen thuộc chỉ để **minh hoạ — giả định** cách áp dụng lý thuyết bài học; **không** mô tả kiến trúc nội bộ đã được công bố và **không** phải phát ngôn đại diện doanh nghiệp.

1. **Shopee (minh hoạ — giả định)**
   - **Tình huống:** Nhiều hostname/region, muốn một lớp edge thống nhất thay vì hàng loạt LB riêng.
   - **Bài toán hệ thống:** TLS + routing theo host/path phải tự động hoá.
   - **Vận dụng lý thuyết:** **Ingress controller** + **Cert-Manager** minh hoạ “một LB, nhiều host” — ví dụ định hướng, không mô tả stack Shopee.

2. **Grab (minh hoạ — giả định)**
   - **Tình huống:** Tách pool node cho tầng edge và tầng compute để tránh tranh CPU.
   - **Bài toán hệ thống:** Latency nhạy cảm với việc chia sẻ node giữa proxy và app.
   - **Vận dụng lý thuyết:** **Node pool** + label/selector như demo DOKS — minh hoạ vận hành, không khẳng định bản đồ region Grab.

3. **GitLab (minh hoạ — giả định)**
   - **Tình huống:** Nhiều tenant/custom domain cần chứng chỉ TLS được cấp tự động.
   - **Bài toán hệ thống:** Không scale được nếu vận hành tay từng cert.
   - **Vận dụng lý thuyết:** **ACME** + controller quản **Certificate CRD** — đúng tinh thần bài học, không mô tả chi tiết GitLab SaaS.
Kubernetes on Cloud: Practical Deployment with DigitalOcean
Deploy a NestJS backend + MySQL + Redis on DigitalOcean Kubernetes (DOKS) with NGINX Ingress Controller, Cert-Manager, and Let's Encrypt for real-domain HTTPS automation.

## I. Introduction

Minikube is excellent for learning, but production questions are different:
- How does a request reach your app from the public internet?
- Where is TLS terminated?
- Who handles failover when Pods die?

Building Kubernetes manually on raw VMs is heavy operational work (`kubeadm`, etcd, control-plane HA, cert rotation). Managed Kubernetes (DOKS/EKS/GKE/AKS) offloads control-plane management so teams can focus on workloads and platform controllers.

## II. Essence

Target flow: ***Internet*** -> ***DigitalOcean Load Balancer*** -> ***NGINX Ingress Controller*** -> `backend-service` -> 3 backend Pods -> `mysql-service` / `redis-service`.  
***Cert-Manager*** integrates with ***Let's Encrypt*** to issue and renew TLS certificates.

- ***NGINX Ingress Controller*** (2 replicas): routes HTTPS traffic into the cluster.
- ***Cert-Manager***: automatic certificate issuance and renewal through ACME.
- ***Backend*** (NestJS, 3 replicas): API service with MySQL + Redis.
- ***Client*** access: `https://api.your-domain.com`.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/system-design-mastery/kubernetes-on-cloud)

| Component | Technology | Role | Port / Namespace |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cluster** | DOKS | Managed Kubernetes with dedicated node pools | - |
| **CLI** | `doctl`, `kubectl`, `helm` | Cluster access and deployment tooling | - |
| **Ingress Controller** | NGINX Ingress | HTTPS routing and LB integration | 80 / 443 (`ingress-nginx`) |
| **Cert Manager** | cert-manager | ACME automation for TLS | `cert-manager` |
| **Backend** | NestJS | API server, 3 replicas | 3000 |
| **Database** | MySQL 8.0 | Persistent app data | 3306 |
| **Cache** | Redis 7 | Short-lived cache | 6379 |

```mermaid
graph LR
    Internet((Internet)) --> LB[DO Load Balancer :443]
    LB --> Ingress[NGINX Ingress Controller x2]
    Ingress -->|TLS Termination| SVC[backend-service :3000]
    SVC --> Pod1(Backend Pod 1)
    SVC --> Pod2(Backend Pod 2)
    SVC --> Pod3(Backend Pod 3)
    Pod1 --> MySQL[(mysql-service :3306)]
    Pod1 --> Redis[(redis-service :6379)]
    CertMgr[Cert-Manager] -.->|ACME HTTP-01| Ingress
    CertMgr -.->|Let's Encrypt| LE((Let's Encrypt))
```

### Environment Setup and Installation Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** Prepare all required cloud accounts and tools.
- **2. Clone demo source:**
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/system-design-mastery/4-kubernetes-on-cloud
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Create DOKS cluster:** choose stable Kubernetes version and create node pools (edge/system separation).
- **4. Configure `kubectl`:**
  ```bash
  doctl kubernetes cluster kubeconfig save <cluster-name>
  kubectl get nodes
  ```
- **5. Install cert-manager:**
  ```bash
  cd cert-manager
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  kubectl get pods -n cert-manager
  ```
- **6. Install NGINX ingress controller:**
  ```bash
  cd ../nginx-ingress-controller
  chmod +x run.sh && ./run.sh
  kubectl get svc -n ingress-nginx -w
  ```
- **7. Point DNS A record to ingress external IP.**
- **8. Apply issuer + data tier + backend + ingress:**
  ```bash
  kubectl apply -f cluster-issuer.yaml
  kubectl apply -f mysql-pod.yaml
  kubectl apply -f mysql-service.yaml
  kubectl apply -f redis-pod.yaml
  kubectl apply -f redis-service.yaml
  kubectl apply -f backend-deployment.yaml
  kubectl apply -f backend-service.yaml
  kubectl apply -f ingress.yaml
  ```
- **9. Verify status:**
  ```bash
  kubectl get pods
  kubectl get ingress
  kubectl get certificate
  ```

### Application Testing

- **Step 1 - Certificate readiness:**
  ```bash
  kubectl get certificate
  kubectl describe certificate backend-tls-secret
  ```
- **Step 2 - HTTPS health check:**
  ```bash
  curl -s https://api.your-domain.com/health
  ```
- **Step 3 - Create data over HTTPS:**
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST https://api.your-domain.com/items \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"digitalocean"}'
  ```
- **Step 4 - Verify cache flow:**
  ```bash
  curl -s https://api.your-domain.com/items
  curl -s https://api.your-domain.com/items
  ```

## III. Core Concepts

- ***Managed Kubernetes***: cloud provider manages control plane, team manages workloads.
- ***Ingress***: host/path routing layer in front of services.
- ***Ingress Controller***: runtime implementation of ingress rules (NGINX).
- ***Cert-Manager***: certificate lifecycle automation via ACME.
- ***ClusterIssuer vs Issuer***: cluster-wide vs namespace-scoped certificate issuers.
- ***HTTP-01 / DNS-01*** challenges: domain ownership verification methods.
- ***Node Pool***: isolated worker groups for workload separation.
- ***TLS Termination***: HTTPS decrypted at ingress, internal traffic continues to backend.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

Scope: Production edge hardening and stateful reliability.

- Use **StatefulSet/PVC** or managed DB services for MySQL/Redis in production.
- Use proper **Secrets** and external secret managers instead of plaintext credentials.
- Define **readiness/liveness probes** and resources to avoid rollout 502s and noisy-neighbor failures.
- Respect Let's Encrypt **rate limits** and use staging issuers during validation.

## V. Applications in Real Systems

Illustrative examples only (not official architecture disclosures):

1. **Shopee (illustrative)** - centralized ingress + automated TLS across many hosts.
2. **Grab (illustrative)** - separate edge and compute node pools for performance isolation.
3. **GitLab (illustrative)** - automated certificate issuance for many domains.

steps.title: Configure Kong API Gateway (DB-less mode)
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create a `kong.yml` (declarative config) file with the following content:
    ```yaml
    _format_version: "3.0"
    services:
      - name: auth-service
        url: http://auth-service:3001
        routes:
          - name: auth-route
            paths:
              - /auth
      - name: product-service
        url: http://product-service:3002
        routes:
          - name: product-route
            paths:
              - /products
    ```
  - Step 2: Verify the file structure follows correct YAML syntax and maps service names to container names in Docker Compose.
- **Expected result:** The `kong.yml` file correctly defines 2 services and 2 corresponding routes.
- **Conclusion:** Kong will read this file on startup to automatically create routing without a database.

steps.title: Create docker-compose.yml and run the system
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create `docker-compose.yml` with 3 services: `auth-service` (build from `./auth-service`), `product-service` (build from `./product-service`), and `kong` (image `kong:3.4`, environment `KONG_DATABASE=off`, `KONG_DECLARATIVE_CONFIG=/etc/kong/kong.yml`, mount `kong.yml` into container).
  - Step 2: Expose Kong port (e.g., `8000:8000`).
  - Step 3: Run the system:
    ```bash
    docker-compose up --build
    ```
- **Expected result:** All 3 containers start successfully, Kong logs show declarative config loaded.
- **Conclusion:** The API Gateway system is ready to receive requests and route them to microservices.

steps.title: Test routing through Kong
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Call the Auth endpoint through Kong:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"username":"admin","password":"123"}'
    ```
  - Step 2: Call the Product endpoint through Kong:
    ```bash
    curl http://localhost:8000/products
    ```
  - Step 3: Call a non-existent path to confirm Kong returns 404:
    ```bash
    curl http://localhost:8000/unknown
    ```
- **Expected result:**
  - `POST /auth/login` through Kong returns `{ token: "fake-jwt-token" }`.
  - `GET /products` through Kong returns the product array.
  - `GET /unknown` returns 404 or a route not found message from Kong.
- **Conclusion:** Kong API Gateway correctly routes requests to the corresponding microservice based on path prefix.

steps.title: Configure Kong with routing and Rate Limiting plugin
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create `kong.yml` defining 3 services (user-service, product-service, order-service) with corresponding routes (`/users`, `/products`, `/orders`).
  - Step 2: Add the `rate-limiting` plugin to `product-service`:
    ```yaml
    plugins:
      - name: rate-limiting
        config:
          minute: 5
          policy: local
    ```
  - Step 3: Run the system and test rate limiting by calling `GET /products` more than 5 times consecutively within 1 minute.
- **Expected result:** The first 5 requests return 200, from the 6th request Kong returns 429 Too Many Requests.
- **Conclusion:** The Rate Limiting plugin works correctly, protecting the service from overload.

  - Bước 1: Tạo file `kong.yml` định nghĩa 3 service (user-service, product-service, order-service) với route tương ứng (`/users`, `/products`, `/orders`).

Configure Kong with routing and Rate Limiting plugin

steps.title: Configure JWT Authentication plugin for Order route
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: In `kong.yml`, create a consumer and JWT credential:
    ```yaml
    consumers:
      - username: app-user
        jwt_secrets:
          - key: my-jwt-key
            secret: my-jwt-secret
            algorithm: HS256
    ```
  - Step 2: Add the `jwt` plugin to `order-service`:
    ```yaml
    plugins:
      - name: jwt
    ```
  - Step 3: Generate a valid JWT token (using the `jsonwebtoken` library or jwt.io) with payload containing `iss: "my-jwt-key"`, signed with secret `my-jwt-secret`.
  - Step 4: Call `POST /orders` without a token to confirm 401 response. Call again with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header to confirm 201 response.
- **Expected result:** Requests without JWT are blocked by Kong with 401. Requests with valid JWT are forwarded to Order Service normally.
- **Conclusion:** The JWT plugin protects sensitive routes, only allowing authenticated requests.

steps.title: Test the entire system
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Run the system:
    ```bash
    docker-compose up --build
    ```
  - Step 2: Test User Service (no plugin):
    ```bash
    curl http://localhost:8000/users
    ```
  - Step 3: Test Rate Limiting on Product Service (call 6 times consecutively):
    ```bash
    for i in $(seq 1 6); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8000/products; done
    ```
  - Step 4: Test JWT on Order Service:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"productId":1,"quantity":2,"userId":1}'
    curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer <valid-token>" -d '{"productId":1,"quantity":2,"userId":1}'
    ```
- **Expected result:**
  - `GET /users` returns user list (200).
  - `GET /products` returns 200 for the first 5 requests, 429 for the 6th.
  - `POST /orders` without token returns 401, with valid token returns 201.
- **Conclusion:** The API Gateway system with 3 microservices, Rate Limiting, and JWT Authentication works correctly.

steps.title: Build the Inventory gRPC Service
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create a NestJS project for Inventory Service:
    ```bash
    nest new inventory-service
    ```
  - Step 2: Install dependencies:
    ```bash
    npm install @nestjs/microservices @grpc/grpc-js @grpc/proto-loader
    ```
  - Step 3: Configure `main.ts` to initialize a gRPC microservice on port 5000, pointing to the `inventory.proto` file.
  - Step 4: Create `InventoryController` implementing methods `getItem` and `listItems` with decorators `@GrpcMethod('InventoryService', 'GetItem')` and `@GrpcMethod('InventoryService', 'ListItems')`.
  - Step 5: Create sample data in the service (at least 3 items with `id`, `name`, `quantity`).
- **Expected result:** Inventory Service starts and listens for gRPC requests on port 5000.
- **Conclusion:** The gRPC backend service is ready to receive requests from the Gateway.

  - Bước 3: Cấu hình `main.ts` để khởi tạo gRPC microservice trên cổng 5000, trỏ đến file `inventory.proto`.
  - Bước 4: Tạo `InventoryController` implement các method `getItem` và `listItems` với decorator `@GrpcMethod('InventoryService', 'GetItem')` và `@GrpcMethod('InventoryService', 'ListItems')`.
  - Bước 5: Tạo dữ liệu mẫu trong service (ít nhất 3 item với `id`, `name`, `quantity`).

steps.title: Build the REST API Gateway
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create a NestJS project for the API Gateway:
    ```bash
    nest new api-gateway
    ```
  - Step 2: Install dependencies:
    ```bash
    npm install @nestjs/microservices @grpc/grpc-js @grpc/proto-loader
    ```
  - Step 3: Create `InventoryModule` in the Gateway, register the gRPC client pointing to `localhost:5000` and the `inventory.proto` file.
  - Step 4: Create `InventoryController` in the Gateway with 2 REST endpoints:
    - `GET /inventory` calls `ListItems` via gRPC and returns JSON.
    - `GET /inventory/:id` calls `GetItem` via gRPC and returns JSON.
  - Step 5: Inject the gRPC client service and use `this.inventoryService.getService()` to call RPC methods.
- **Expected result:** The Gateway starts on port 3000, receives REST requests, and converts them to gRPC calls.
- **Conclusion:** The REST -> gRPC -> Response conversion flow has been established.

  - Bước 4: Tạo `InventoryController` trong Gateway với 2 REST endpoint:

steps.title: Build the Catalog gRPC Service
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create a NestJS project for Catalog Service.
  - Step 2: Install gRPC dependencies and configure `main.ts` to initialize a gRPC server on port 5001.
  - Step 3: Implement `CatalogController` with `@GrpcMethod('CatalogService', 'GetProduct')` returning a product by id (throw error if not found) and `@GrpcMethod('CatalogService', 'ListProducts')` returning a list of sample products (at least 5 products with `id`, `name`, `price`, `stock`).
- **Expected result:** Catalog Service listens on gRPC port 5001 and returns correct product data.
- **Conclusion:** Catalog Service is ready to serve both the Gateway and Order Service.

  - Bước 3: Implement `CatalogController` với `@GrpcMethod('CatalogService', 'GetProduct')` trả sản phẩm theo id (ném lỗi nếu không tồn tại) và `@GrpcMethod('CatalogService', 'ListProducts')` trả danh sách sản phẩm mẫu (ít nhất 5 sản phẩm với `id`, `name`, `price`, `stock`).

- **Kết luận:** Catalog Service sẵn sàng phục vụ cả Gateway và Order Service.

steps.title: Build Order gRPC Service with callback to Catalog
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create a NestJS project for Order Service.
  - Step 2: Configure `main.ts` to initialize a gRPC server on port 5002.
  - Step 3: In Order Service, register a gRPC client connecting to Catalog Service (`localhost:5001`, using `catalog.proto`).
  - Step 4: Implement `CreateOrder`: before creating an order, call `GetProduct` to Catalog Service to:
    - Verify the product exists (if not, return gRPC status `NOT_FOUND`).
    - Check `stock >= quantity` (if insufficient, return `FAILED_PRECONDITION`).
    - Calculate `totalPrice = price * quantity`.
  - Step 5: Save the order to an in-memory array and return `OrderResponse` with complete information.
  - Step 6: Implement `ListOrders` returning the list of created orders.
- **Expected result:** Order Service validates products via Catalog before creating orders, responds correctly on success or failure.
- **Conclusion:** Bidirectional gRPC flow between Order and Catalog has been established.

  - Bước 3: Trong Order Service, đăng ký gRPC client kết nối đến Catalog Service (`localhost:5001`, dùng `catalog.proto`).
  - Bước 4: Implement `CreateOrder`: trước khi tạo đơn hàng, gọi `GetProduct` đến Catalog Service để:
    - Kiểm tra sản phẩm có tồn tại không (nếu không, trả lỗi gRPC với status `NOT_FOUND`).
    - Kiểm tra `stock >= quantity` (nếu không đủ, trả lỗi `FAILED_PRECONDITION`).

steps.title: Build the REST API Gateway
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create a NestJS project for the API Gateway.
  - Step 2: Register 2 gRPC clients: one connecting to Catalog Service (port 5001), one connecting to Order Service (port 5002).
  - Step 3: Create REST endpoints:
    - `GET /catalog` -> calls `ListProducts`.
    - `GET /catalog/:id` -> calls `GetProduct`.
    - `POST /orders` (body: `{ productId, quantity, customerName }`) -> calls `CreateOrder`.
    - `GET /orders` -> calls `ListOrders`.
  - Step 4: Handle gRPC errors (NOT_FOUND, FAILED_PRECONDITION) and convert them to appropriate HTTP status codes (404, 400).
- **Expected result:** Gateway exposes 4 REST endpoints, correctly converts between REST and gRPC, handles errors appropriately.
- **Conclusion:** The Gateway acts as an intermediary, hiding the gRPC protocol from clients.

steps.title: Test the bidirectional flow and error handling
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Start Catalog Service, Order Service, and API Gateway sequentially.
  - Step 2: Get the product list:
    ```bash
    curl http://localhost:3000/catalog
    ```
  - Step 3: Create a successful order:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"productId":1,"quantity":2,"customerName":"Minh"}'
    ```
  - Step 4: Create an order with a non-existent product:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"productId":999,"quantity":1,"customerName":"Minh"}'
    ```
  - Step 5: Create an order with quantity exceeding stock:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"productId":1,"quantity":99999,"customerName":"Minh"}'
    ```
  - Step 6: Get the list of created orders:
    ```bash
    curl http://localhost:3000/orders
    ```
- **Expected result:**
  - `GET /catalog` returns the product list.
  - `POST /orders` with valid data returns an order with correctly calculated `totalPrice`.
  - `POST /orders` with non-existent `productId` returns 404.
  - `POST /orders` with `quantity` exceeding `stock` returns 400.
  - `GET /orders` returns the list of successfully created orders.
- **Conclusion:** The bidirectional flow works correctly: Gateway -> Order -> Catalog (validate) -> Order (create) -> Gateway (return result).

steps.title: Set up Kafka with Docker Compose
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create `docker-compose.yml` with Kafka running in KRaft mode (no Zookeeper needed):
    ```yaml
    services:
      kafka:
        image: bitnami/kafka:3.6
        environment:
          - KAFKA_CFG_NODE_ID=1
          - KAFKA_CFG_PROCESS_ROLES=broker,controller
          - KAFKA_CFG_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093
          - KAFKA_CFG_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093
          - KAFKA_CFG_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092
          - KAFKA_CFG_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES=CONTROLLER
          - KAFKA_CFG_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP=CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT,PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT
        ports:
          - "9092:9092"
    ```
  - Step 2: Start Kafka:
    ```bash
    docker-compose up -d kafka
    ```
- **Expected result:** Kafka broker starts successfully on port 9092.
- **Conclusion:** The messaging infrastructure is ready for services to connect.

    ```bash
    nest new payment-service
    ```
  - Step 2: Install dependencies:
    ```bash
    npm install @nestjs/microservices kafkajs
    ```
  - Step 3: Register a Kafka client in the module using `ClientsModule.register()`, configure broker `kafka:9092`.

- **Expected result:** Each time `POST /payments` is called, a message is sent to the Kafka topic `payment-events`.
- **Conclusion:** The Producer is ready to emit events for consumers to process.

steps.title: Test broadcasting and Consumer Groups
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Run the entire system (Kafka + 3 services):
    ```bash
    docker-compose up --build
    ```
  - Step 2: Send a payment request:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/payments -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"orderId":101,"amount":250000,"method":"credit_card"}'
    ```
  - Step 3: Check the Shipping Service log: should contain `[Shipping] Processing shipment for order 101`.
  - Step 4: Check the Notification Service log: should contain `[Notification] Sending payment confirmation for order 101`.
  - Step 5: Send 2-3 more requests to confirm every event is processed by both consumers.
- **Expected result:**
  - Every `PAYMENT_COMPLETED` event is received and processed by both Shipping Service and Notification Service.
  - Logs from both services display independently, proving different Consumer Groups each receive the message.
- **Conclusion:** The broadcasting mechanism via Consumer Groups in Kafka works correctly: each group receives a copy of the message, ensuring each domain processes its own business logic.

    ```bash
    docker-compose up --build
    ```
  - Bước 2: Gửi request thanh toán:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/payments -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"orderId":101,"amount":250000,"method":"credit_card"}'
    ```
  - Bước 3: Kiểm tra log của Shipping Service: phải có dòng `[Shipping] Processing shipment for order 101`.
  - Bước 4: Kiểm tra log của Notification Service: phải có dòng `[Notification] Sending payment confirmation for order 101`.
  - Bước 5: Gửi thêm 2-3 request để xác nhận mỗi sự kiện đều được cả 2 consumer xử lý.
- **Kết quả mong đợi:**
  - Mỗi `PAYMENT_COMPLETED` event được cả Shipping Service và Notification Service nhận và xử lý.
  - Log của 2 service hiển thị độc lập, chứng minh Consumer Groups khác nhau đều nhận được message.
- **Kết luận:** Cơ chế broadcasting qua Consumer Groups trong Kafka hoạt động đúng: mỗi group nhận bản sao của message, đảm bảo mỗi domain xử lý nghiệp vụ riêng.

challenges.title: Advanced Event-Driven: Dead Letter Queue, Retry, and Consumer Recovery
challenges.description: Extend the event-driven system with Kafka to handle failure scenarios: implement a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) mechanism when a consumer fails to process, demonstrate consumer recovery when offline (Kafka persistent log), and add basic retry logic before sending messages to the DLQ.
challenges.requirements: Build a NestJS system with Kafka consisting of: `PaymentService` (Producer) emitting `PAYMENT_COMPLETED` events, `FulfillmentService` (Consumer) processing events with retry logic (max 3 attempts), sending failed messages to DLQ topic `payment-events-dlq` after exhausting retries. Add `DlqMonitorService` to read and log messages from the DLQ. Demonstrate Kafka persistent log by stopping the consumer, sending events, restarting the consumer, and confirming the consumer still receives the missed messages.

steps.title: Implement Fulfillment Service with Retry and DLQ
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create a handler listening to topic `payment-events` with `@EventPattern('PAYMENT_COMPLETED')`.
  - Step 2: Implement retry logic: when receiving a message, check `shouldFail`. If `true`, increment `retryCount` and retry (max 3 times).
  - Step 3: Store `retryCount` in metadata or in the payload (add a `retryCount` field when re-emitting).
  - Step 4: After 3 failed attempts, send the original message to DLQ topic `payment-events-dlq` with error information:
    ```json
    {
      "originalPayload": { "orderId": 101, "amount": 250000 },
      "error": "Processing failed after 3 retries",
      "failedAt": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "retryCount": 3
    }
    ```
  - Step 5: If processing succeeds (shouldFail = false), log: `[Fulfillment] Order ${orderId} fulfilled successfully`.
- **Expected result:** Successful messages are processed normally, failed messages are retried 3 times then moved to the DLQ.
- **Conclusion:** The retry and DLQ mechanism ensures no messages are lost and errors are isolated.

  - Bước 3: Lưu `retryCount` trong metadata hoặc trong payload (thêm trường `retryCount` khi re-emit).
  - Bước 4: Sau 3 lần thất bại, gửi message gốc vào topic DLQ `payment-events-dlq` kèm thông tin lỗi:

    ```json
      "retryCount": 3
    }
    ```
  - Bước 5: Nếu xử lý thành công (shouldFail = false), log: `[Fulfillment] Order ${orderId} fulfilled successfully`.
- **Kết quả mong đợi:** Message thành công được xử lý bình thường, message thất bại được retry 3 lần rồi chuyển vào DLQ.

steps.title: Implement DLQ Monitor Service
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Configure DLQ Monitor Service to listen to topic `payment-events-dlq` with `groupId: 'dlq-monitor-group'`.
  - Step 2: Create a handler to read messages from the DLQ and log details: `[DLQ Monitor] Failed message - orderId: ${orderId}, error: ${error}, retryCount: ${retryCount}`.
  - Step 3: (Optional) Store DLQ messages in an in-memory array and expose endpoint `GET /dlq/messages` for inspection.
- **Expected result:** DLQ Monitor receives and logs every failed message from the DLQ topic.
- **Conclusion:** DLQ Monitor enables monitoring and manual handling of failed messages.

steps.title: Build the User Service (Publisher)
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create a NestJS project:
    ```bash
    nest new user-service
    ```
  - Step 2: Install the Redis client:
    ```bash
    npm install ioredis
    ```
  - Step 3: Create a `RedisModule` registering a Redis client (connecting to `redis:6379`) and exporting it for other modules to use.
  - Step 4: Create `UserController` with endpoint `POST /users/register` accepting body `{ name, email }`.
  - Step 5: In the handler, after processing registration (mock), publish a message to Redis channel `user-events`:
    ```typescript
    this.redisClient.publish('user-events', JSON.stringify({
      event: 'USER_REGISTERED',
      data: { name, email, registeredAt: new Date().toISOString() }
    }));
    ```
- **Expected result:** Each time `POST /users/register` is called, a message is published to Redis channel `user-events`.
- **Conclusion:** The Publisher is ready to emit events in a fire-and-forget manner.

steps.title: Demonstrate fire-and-forget and test
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Run the entire system (Redis + 3 services):
    ```bash
    docker-compose up --build
    ```
  - Step 2: Send a user registration request:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/users/register -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name":"Minh","email":"minh@example.com"}'
    ```
  - Step 3: Check logs of Welcome Email Service and Activity Log Service: both should receive the event.
  - Step 4: Stop Activity Log Service (docker-compose stop activity-log-service).
  - Step 5: Send another registration request:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/users/register -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name":"Lan","email":"lan@example.com"}'
    ```
  - Step 6: Restart Activity Log Service and check logs: the message sent while offline will NOT be received.
- **Expected result:**
  - When both subscribers are online: both receive the event.
  - When Activity Log is offline: only Welcome Email receives it, Activity Log loses the message.
  - When Activity Log restarts: it does NOT receive the lost message (fire-and-forget).
- **Conclusion:** Redis Pub/Sub is fire-and-forget: messages are only delivered to subscribers that are online at the time of publishing, with no persistent storage like Kafka.

Use Docker Compose to run both Redis and Kafka. Write documentation explaining the reasoning behind pattern choices for each scenario.

steps.title: Set up Kafka and Redis with Docker Compose
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create `docker-compose.yml` with both Kafka (KRaft mode) and Redis:
    ```yaml
    services:
      kafka:
        image: bitnami/kafka:3.6
        environment:
          - KAFKA_CFG_NODE_ID=1
          - KAFKA_CFG_PROCESS_ROLES=broker,controller
          - KAFKA_CFG_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093
          - KAFKA_CFG_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093
          - KAFKA_CFG_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092
          - KAFKA_CFG_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES=CONTROLLER
          - KAFKA_CFG_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP=CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT,PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT
        ports:
          - "9092:9092"
      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - "6379:6379"
    ```
  - Step 2: Start the infrastructure:
    ```bash
    docker-compose up -d kafka redis
    ```
- **Expected result:** Both Kafka and Redis start successfully.
- **Conclusion:** Dual messaging infrastructure is ready for both patterns.

steps.title: Build the Order Service (Dual Publisher)
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create a NestJS project for Order Service.
  - Step 2: Install dependencies:
    ```bash
    npm install @nestjs/microservices kafkajs ioredis
    ```
  - Step 3: Register both the Kafka client and Redis client in the module.
  - Step 4: Create `OrderController` with endpoint `POST /orders` accepting body `{ productId, quantity, customerName }`.
  - Step 5: In the handler, when an order is created successfully:
    - Send `ORDER_CREATED` event to **Kafka** topic `order-events` (critical event, guaranteed delivery):
      ```typescript
      this.kafkaClient.emit('ORDER_CREATED', { orderId, productId, quantity, customerName, createdAt });
      ```
    - Send notification to **Redis** channel `order-notifications` (real-time, fire-and-forget):
      ```typescript
      this.redisClient.publish('order-notifications', JSON.stringify({ type: 'NEW_ORDER', orderId, customerName }));
      ```
- **Expected result:** Every order creation sends events simultaneously to Kafka (persistent) and Redis (real-time).
- **Conclusion:** Order Service uses the right pattern for the right purpose: Kafka for critical data, Redis for instant notifications.

    ```bash
    npm install @nestjs/microservices kafkajs ioredis
    ```
  - Bước 3: Đăng ký cả Kafka client và Redis client trong module.
  - Bước 4: Tạo `OrderController` với endpoint `POST /orders` nhận body `{ productId, quantity, customerName }`.
  - Bước 5: Trong handler, khi tạo đơn hàng thành công:
    - Gửi sự kiện `ORDER_CREATED` lên **Kafka** topic `order-events` (sự kiện quan trọng, cần đảm bảo delivery):
      ```typescript
      this.kafkaClient.emit('ORDER_CREATED', { orderId, productId, quantity, customerName, createdAt });
      ```
    - Gửi thông báo lên **Redis** channel `order-notifications` (thông báo real-time, fire-and-forget):
      ```typescript
      this.redisClient.publish('order-notifications', JSON.stringify({ type: 'NEW_ORDER', orderId, customerName }));
      ```
- **Kết quả mong đợi:** Mỗi khi tạo đơn hàng, sự kiện được gửi đồng thời lên Kafka (persistent) và Redis (real-time).
- **Kết luận:** Order Service sử dụng đúng pattern cho đúng mục đích: Kafka cho dữ liệu quan trọng, Redis cho thông báo tức thời.
